findings.description: Five systems — process_pending_damage_effects (line 173), update_fire_dot (174), update_electric_charge (175), update_electric_arc_visuals (176), and update_persistent_effect_visuals (181) — run every gameplay frame without any_with_component guards. All neighbouring systems in the same add_systems block (update_poisoned, update_sickened, emit_burning_unit_vfx) already have such guards, making this an incomplete optimization pass that iterates empty queries unconditionally each frame.
findings.recommendation: Add run_if(any_with_component::<PendingDamageEffect>) to process_pending_damage_effects, run_if(any_with_component::<FireDoT>) to update_fire_dot, run_if(any_with_component::<Shocked>) to update_electric_charge, run_if(any_with_component::<ElectricArcVisual>) to update_electric_arc_visuals, and a suitable disjunctive condition for update_persistent_effect_visuals.

findings.description: update_timed_modifier::<TemporaryHitPoints>, update_timed_modifier::<SlowMovementModifier>, update_timed_modifier::<RootedModifier>, and update_timed_modifier::<HasteModifier> (lines 80–85) lack any_with_component guards, while update_timed_modifier::<Stunned> on line 86 has one. All analogous calls in the block at lines 208–221 also have guards. The four ungated calls iterate empty queries every frame once those effects expire.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(any_with_component::<TemporaryHitPoints>) and corresponding guards to the other three ungated timed-modifier registrations, consistent with the rest of the block.

findings.description: At 570 LOC, status_effects.rs exceeds the project 300-LOC limit by nearly 2x and is not a single-match or registry monolith. It mixes five distinct concern groups: (1) simple CCs — Stunned, RootedModifier, FrozenSolidModifier, Petrified, FearModifier; (2) sleep — SleepModifier plus four sub-components (NightTerrors, Comatose, NarcolepticWave, Sleepwalking); (3) combat buffs — BattleHymnModifier with EchoingSong/AnthemResilience, BerserkerRageModifier; (4) stat debuffs — PoisonedModifier, SickenedModifier, SmellyModifier; (5) transformation/warping — PolymorphedModifier, BanishedModifier, WasBanished.
findings.recommendation: Split into cc_effects.rs, sleep.rs, buffs.rs, poison.rs, and transformation.rs, re-exporting all types from the existing components/mod.rs to preserve import paths.

findings.description: impl_timed_modifier!(SmellyModifier) is called inside status_effects.rs (line 525), but all other impl_timed_modifier! invocations are centralized in components/mod.rs (lines 71–85). The two-site split is confusing and makes it easy to omit the macro call when adding future status-effect types.
findings.recommendation: Move impl_timed_modifier!(SmellyModifier) into the existing block in components/mod.rs.

findings.description: Module doc says 'Contains all game unit types: wizard, infantry, and archers.' The module now contains 14+ distinct unit types including boss, brute, commander, assassin, aerialist, healer, shielder, dispeller, teleporter, elite, and undead.
findings.recommendation: Update the module doc comment to reflect the current full scope.

findings.description: DamageType::Necrotic has the comment 'reserved for future spells' but is actively used by FingerOfDeath, RaiseTheDead, and MarkOfDeath (wizard/spell_enum.rs:538–550).
findings.recommendation: Update the doc comment to list the spells that actually deal Necrotic damage.

findings.description: The function is named update_electric_charge but the component it processes is Shocked. Every other update_* system in the module is named after its component (update_fire_dot processes FireDoT, update_poisoned processes PoisonedModifier, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Rename the function to update_shocked, or rename the Shocked component to ElectricCharge to align naming across the codebase.

findings.description: 536-line file mixes five distinct concerns: lifecycle cleanup (cleanup_game, cleanup_for_replay, reset_resources_for_replay, init_level_from_config, apply_game_speed, auto_pause_on_focus_loss), gameplay ticks (tick_attack_cycle, tick_elapsed_time, calculate_effectiveness, activate_defenders_on_proximity), audio ambience (load_battle_ambience_assets, update_battle_ambience, update_crowd_ambience, stop_all_sfx), shadow rendering (ShadowMaterial, ShadowAssets, preload_shadow_assets, spawn_terrain_shadow, spawn_unit_shadows, update_unit_shadows), and achievement tracking (track_wizard_enemy_damage, wizard_has_not_damaged_enemies). Project conventions require files >300 LOC to be split unless cohesive.
findings.recommendation: Split into ambience.rs (~130 LOC: audio resources + systems), shadows.rs (~120 LOC: ShadowMaterial + shadow systems), lifecycle.rs (~90 LOC: cleanup + reset + apply_game_speed + auto_pause_on_focus_loss), keeping shared_systems.rs for the remaining gameplay cross-cuts (~180 LOC).

findings.description: The matches! arm 'MultiplayerGameState::Running | Paused | Settings | SpellBook | CauldronMenu' is copy-pasted verbatim in three separate functions: is_gameplay_running (line 88), is_local_wizard_active (line 138), and is_spell_effects_active (line 172). Adding a new MultiplayerGameState variant requires updating all three independently, a latent divergence risk.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private fn mp_game_state_is_active(state: &MultiplayerGameState) -> bool { matches!(state, Running | Paused | ...) } and call it from all three functions.

findings.description: WaveSpawnedMessage is registered in plugin.rs:63, written in wave_systems.rs:221, but has zero MessageReader subscribers anywhere in the codebase. The wave_number field carries #[allow(dead_code)] confirming it is never consumed. This is a dead message channel that adds unnecessary noise and a per-frame message buffer.
findings.recommendation: Either add a UI consumer (wave-number HUD indicator) to justify the channel, or remove the message type, its add_message registration, and the MessageWriter parameter from tick_wave_timer.

findings.description: cleanup_game (line 125) and cleanup_for_replay (line 139) have identical bodies: both despawn all OnGameplayScreen entities. They differ only in their doc-comment and query variable name. Two identical fns registered to different schedule hooks will silently diverge on future changes.
findings.recommendation: Keep both public fns (they serve different schedule hooks), but have each delegate to a single private fn despawn_all_gameplay_entities(commands, query) helper.

findings.description: KillStats::reset() manually zeros all 10 fields, duplicating the logic already implied by #[derive(Default)] on the same struct. If a new field is added to the struct but not to reset(), the reset silently leaves stale data across replays.
findings.recommendation: Replace the body of reset() with *self = Default::default(); so the two code paths are structurally equivalent.

findings.description: calculate_effectiveness builds a Vec<_> snapshot of all unit data on every gameplay frame and then runs an O(n^2) comparison loop. With ~200+ units at higher levels (100 defenders + 60+ infantry + archers + bosses) this is ~40,000 distance checks and one 200-element heap allocation per frame at 60fps. No comment documents this as an accepted trade-off.
findings.recommendation: Consider throttling to every 4-8 frames via a frame-counter resource (effectiveness changes slowly), or add a spatial hash using the existing pathfinding grid. At minimum, add a doc comment noting the O(n^2) cost and acknowledged unit-cap ceiling.

findings.description: BATTLE_AMBIENCE_MAX_DISTANCE = 10000.0 is a file-local constant whose value is duplicated by MAX_SFX_DISTANCE = 10000.0 in units/wizard/spells/audio.rs:12. Two independent constants with the same value and the same physical meaning will diverge on tuning.
findings.recommendation: Define a single pub const MAX_WORLD_SFX_DISTANCE: f32 = 10000.0; in constants/tuning.rs and reference it from both files.

findings.description: toggle_debug_ui_visible is registered with .add_systems(Update, toggle_debug_ui_visible) with no run_if state guard. Per project conventions every Update system must have a run_if guard. It currently processes keyboard events in all app states including main menu and loading screens.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(in_state(AppState::InGame).or(in_state(AppState::MultiplayerGame))) or at minimum .run_if(not(in_state(AppState::Loading))) to match the F2 debug-UI convention.

findings.description: Grease is grouped in the Burning arm of status_effects(), so the spell book displays Burning as its primary effect. The spell description (line 329) and implementation (spells/grease/casting/slow.rs) make clear that slowing is the primary effect; burning only occurs when a fire spell ignites the grease pool. Players reading the spell book are misled about what the spell does.
findings.recommendation: Move Grease out of the Burning arm and give it &[StatusEffectKind::Slowed]. Leave the ignition-only Burning undocumented (matching the existing convention for secondary interactions) or add a comment noting it.

findings.description: WallOfStone is placed under the comment '// Root spells (immediately researchable)' with research_cost = 30, but its prerequisite() (line 623) returns Some(Spell::SpikeGrowth), which itself costs 60 and is second-tier. WallOfStone cannot be researched until SpikeGrowth is unlocked, so the comment and implied cost tier are wrong.
findings.recommendation: Fix the comment to reflect WallOfStone's second-tier status. Consider raising research_cost to the 50–60 range to match its tree depth.

findings.description: required_total_spells() always returns 0 with the comment 'All spells are now in prerequisite chains; no gate requirements needed.' Two UI files (study_tab/panels/helpers.rs:47, spell_detail.rs:229) still call it and branch on its value, doing permanently dead work.
findings.recommendation: Delete required_total_spells() and its two UI call sites if the feature is retired, or mark it #[deprecated] with a note explaining its dormant state.

findings.description: talent_cast_time_multiplier() is a private helper in runtime.rs that only handles Spell::BlackHole. It reaches across module boundaries to import black_hole_constants::QUICK_COLLAPSE_CAST_TIME_MULT. As new talent cast-time modifiers are added, this function will accumulate arms coupling the wizard runtime to individual spell constant modules.
findings.recommendation: Consider embedding each spell's talent cast-time override in the spell's own constants file, accessed via primed_config() or a dedicated method, so runtime.rs does not grow a per-spell match.

findings.description: pulse_spell_range_indicator runs every Update frame and calls materials.get_mut(handle) unconditionally, which marks the asset dirty every frame. The alpha_mode field is set every frame but never changes after spawn.
findings.recommendation: Drop the alpha_mode write (it is invariant after setup). Consider only calling get_mut when the computed alpha has changed by more than a small epsilon to avoid spurious dirty marks.

findings.description: Comment '// Thin ring, 5 units wide (half of previous 10)' is a developer changelog note embedded in source code. It will become stale if the value changes again.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a purpose-oriented comment: '// ring cross-section thickness in world units'.

findings.description: spawn_range_circle computes initial_scale = actual_ground_radius / base_ground_radius. If the wizard spawns at y >= BASE_HEIGHT (100.0), base_ground_radius can be zero or negative (from ground_projected_range), producing NaN or inf scale with no guard.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard before the division: if base_ground_radius <= 0.0 { return; }.

findings.description: spawn_weather_particles allocates new mesh and material assets via meshes.add()/materials.add() on every frame it runs. Rain spawns a new Rectangle mesh + StandardMaterial per batch call; snow similarly. This creates fresh Bevy asset store entries each frame, triggering change detection unnecessarily. The project standard is to pre-cache particle shapes in SpellVisualAssets (see particle_quad at visual_assets.rs:865).
findings.recommendation: Extract rain and snow mesh + material handles into a MeteorologistPlugin OnEnter setup (or a dedicated WeatherVisualAssets resource), cache them at game start, and clone the handles per particle spawn.

findings.description: spawn_weather_overlays carries the doc comment 'Applies the Drought healing reduction to a heal amount. Returns the (possibly reduced) heal amount.' — a verbatim copy from state.rs::apply_dry_healing_reduction. Completely incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc: 'Spawns the fullscreen sky-tint UI overlay node used by all weather conditions.'

findings.description: storm_lightning carries the same wrong doc comment 'Applies the Drought healing reduction to a heal amount.' — another copy/paste artifact from the drought helper. The function actually performs random lightning strikes with AoE splash.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc summarizing the function: random lightning strike on a living unit, AoE splash damage, visual beam spawn.

findings.description: targets.iter().len() iterates all living entities to count (O(n)), then targets.iter_mut().nth(target_index) iterates again up to the selected index (O(n) worst case). Two full scans per strike frame.
findings.recommendation: Collect target entities into a Vec once, then select by random index. Makes intent explicit and avoids the double iteration.

findings.description: BASE_SPELL_RANGE is defined as a function-local const with value 3000.0 — identical to wizard::constants::DEFAULT_SPELL_RANGE. Two definitions of the same tuning constant silently diverge if one is changed.
findings.recommendation: Replace the local const with a use of crate::game::units::wizard::constants::DEFAULT_SPELL_RANGE.

findings.description: spread_shock_to_wet (shock propagation damage logic) lives in state.rs alongside weather-input handling and timer ticking. The file name implies state management but it mixes a damage-propagation concern.
findings.recommendation: Move spread_shock_to_wet to effects.rs where the other damage-dealing weather effects live (storm_lightning, update_burning_patches). Low priority — file is under 300 LOC.

findings.description: definitions/mod.rs defines the TalentDefinition struct (lines 12-22) and the talent_definitions() dispatch function (lines 26-59), violating the project rule that mod.rs does only 'mod' declarations and 'pub use' re-exports. No logic or type definitions belong here.
findings.recommendation: Move TalentDefinition struct and talent_definitions() into a sibling file (e.g. definitions/registry.rs or definitions/dispatcher.rs). Reduce mod.rs to pure mod declarations and pub(crate) use re-exports.

findings.description: The talent name for the Magic Missile tier-2 'Arcane Barrage' talent is sourced from crate::game::units::wizard::spells::magic_missile::constants::ARCANE_BARRAGE_NAME rather than a string literal. This couples the talent definition layer to the spell's internal constant module. If the constant is renamed for spell-system reasons the talent display changes silently, and the coupling is unexpected for anyone reading the talent definitions file.
findings.recommendation: Use a string literal directly in force.rs. Talent display data should be self-contained. If the name must stay consistent with the spell system, add a comment explaining why the constant is referenced.

findings.description: TalentDefinition.implemented: bool is marked #[allow(dead_code)] because it is never read anywhere in the codebase. It is set to true in all 270 (31 spells × 9 talent slots) struct literals and never set to false. The field was presumably a development scaffold to track unimplemented talent effects, but it is now a no-op that adds noise to every definition block.
findings.recommendation: Remove the implemented field from TalentDefinition and delete all 270 'implemented: true' literals. The #[allow(dead_code)] suppression can be removed at the same time. If an 'unimplemented' signal is needed in future, use a dedicated enum variant or a conditional compilation flag rather than a boolean in display data.

findings.description: The save-file HashMap key for spell talent selections is constructed as format!("{:?}", spell), which couples the persistent key to Spell's Debug representation. If Spell gains a custom Debug impl, a #[debug = ...] attribute, or a variant is renamed, the on-disk keys silently stop matching and all player talent selections for that spell are lost without any error. The same pattern is used in wizard_crud.rs (out of this scope) but the fragile key construction originates here in the validation path of ActiveTalents::from_save.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a Spell::save_key(&self) -> &'static str method (an exhaustive match returning stable string literals) and use it everywhere HashMap keys are constructed for talent data. This is the same pattern the UI uses for spell display names and is already established in the project.

findings.description: Six talent names are shared across multiple different spells: 'Chain Reaction' appears in both chain_lightning (tier 3) and lightning_rod (tier 2); 'Overcharge' appears in both chain_lightning (tier 2) and lightning_rod (tier 2); 'Magnetic Pull' in both chain_lightning (tier 2, electric.rs) and telekinesis (tier 2, force.rs); 'Scorched Earth' in both fireball (tier 3, fire.rs) and wall_of_fire (tier 2, fire.rs); 'Lingering Flames' in both fireball (tier 1) and grease (tier 2, nature.rs); 'Dimensional Rift' in both black_hole (tier 3, force.rs) and teleport (tier 3, utility.rs). These are functionally independent but identical names create player confusion in the study tab UI.
findings.recommendation: Give each colliding talent a unique, spell-contextual name. Example: 'Lightning Chain Reaction' vs 'Rod Chain Reaction', or choose thematically distinct names. No code change needed — string edits only in the definition files.

findings.description: Spell::Fireball => [1, 2, 3] sets tier thresholds three orders of magnitude lower than comparable damage spells (MagicMissile: [50, 400, 1000]; ChainLightning: [30, 100, 300]; MeteorFall: [20, 70, 200]). With thresholds of 1/2/3, a player unlocks all three Fireball talent tiers on the very first cast. This may be intentional design (Fireball as a 'starter spell'), but it is undocumented and visually indistinguishable from a forgotten placeholder value.
findings.recommendation: If intentional, add a comment: '// Fireball tiers unlock immediately by design — it is the introductory spell.' If accidental, set thresholds comparable to other offense spells (e.g. [20, 75, 200]).

findings.description: BattleTalentProgress::flush_to_save() iterates prev_values returned by add_spell_talent_progress_batch. If save I/O fails and prev_values is empty while self.progress is non-empty, the method silently returns an empty crossed-tiers vec. The caller (achievements/helpers.rs:119) loops silently over nothing, so tier-unlock notifications and save writes are lost without any log line.
findings.recommendation: Add a warn!() when prev_values is empty but self.progress is non-empty, indicating a probable I/O failure: warn!("flush_to_save: prev_values is empty despite {} pending progress entries; tier unlocks may be lost", self.progress.len());

findings.description: VsyncMode::Adaptive doc says 'falls back to off if frame rate drops' but apply_vsync_config (systems.rs:131) maps both Adaptive and On to PresentMode::AutoVsync. The two variants are behaviourally identical.
findings.recommendation: Either map Adaptive to PresentMode::Immediate or update the doc to 'same as On on this backend (Bevy 0.18 removed PresentMode::Adaptive)'.

findings.description: Plugin doc comment says 'Persists changes to disk after 0.5s of inactivity' but SaveDebounceTimer::default() creates a 2.0-second timer (config_file.rs:129).
findings.recommendation: Fix the plugin doc comment to '2.0s of inactivity'.

findings.description: Field doc says 'restored on game start after page reload' — a stale WASM/localStorage era comment. The game has been native-only since March 2026.
findings.recommendation: Update to 'reset at startup; populated when a wizard is loaded'.

findings.description: Four doc comments across save_structs.rs:14, messages.rs:3, messages.rs:13, and progress.rs:149 still reference 'localStorage' from the WASM era. The game is native-only.
findings.recommendation: Replace every 'localStorage' with 'disk' or 'save file'.

findings.description: validate_action_bar_slots (line 171) calls load_unified_save() independently, but its only caller load_wizard_type_into_config already loaded the save via get_wizard_by_type. This is a redundant second cache-clone per wizard load.
findings.recommendation: Accept the already-loaded unlocked_spells as a parameter so validate_action_bar_slots never needs to re-load the save.

findings.description: increment_levels_completed, increment_games_played, and accumulate_kill_stats each perform their own load_unified_save -> save_unified cycle. At battle-end (achievements/helpers.rs:64-72) all three are called sequentially, producing 3 separate cache-clone+store cycles for one logical event.
findings.recommendation: Introduce record_battle_ended_counters(victory, defenders, attackers, undead) that does one load + all mutations + one save, then update the achievements helper to call it.

findings.description: Five systems (detect_window_resize, detect_window_move, detect_game_config_changes, detect_input_bindings_changes, mark_save_on_config_changed) run unconditionally every Update frame with no run_if guard, violating the project convention that every Update system must have one.
findings.recommendation: Gate the group with .run_if(not(in_state(AppState::Splash)).and(not(in_state(AppState::Loading)))) or similar. The systems are internally cheap but the convention gap is a maintenance signal.

findings.description: UNIFIED_SAVE_FILENAME is 'saves_v2.json' but the content is obfuscated TOML serialised to base64, not JSON. Misleads anyone inspecting the file on disk.
findings.recommendation: Rename to 'saves_v2.dat' with a one-time startup migration shim to move the old filename, or add a prominent comment explaining the .json extension is historical.

findings.description: SaveDebounceTimer and SavedWindowedGeometry are pure runtime resources with no serialisation concern, yet they live in config_file.rs whose stated purpose is 'only used for serialisation'.
findings.recommendation: Move them to a new resources/runtime.rs or into systems.rs which is their only consumer.

findings.description: SaveMetadata::version is written as 2 on every new save but is never read to drive or gate any migration. Migrations use file-existence checks instead. The field implies a versioning contract that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Either wire version-gated migration logic and document the increment protocol, or remove the field to avoid implying a false safety net.

findings.description: apply_state_snapshot is a 726-LOC single function handling spawn, update, despawn, material swap, status-flag sync, polymorph restore, smelly/melee/mark mirroring, arrow respawn, and combat animation — all in one body. Every new ghost-side flag extension adds another branch here.
findings.recommendation: Split into concern-named helpers: update_ghost_transforms, sync_ghost_status_flags, sync_ghost_visuals (polymorph/corpse/material), despawn_stale_ghosts, respawn_arrows. The outer snapshot loop orchestrates them.

findings.description: forward_status_effects_to_host is a 440-LOC function with 12 separate query parameters and 12 independent iteration loops, one per status effect. Every new status spell requires touching this function. The structure is entirely mechanical repetition alongside the already-generic cleanup_forwarded_marker<T> pattern in plugin.rs.
findings.recommendation: Extract a ForwardableStatus trait with to_network_message(), then drive a generic forward_status<T: ForwardableStatus> system registered once per type — mirroring the cleanup registration block already in plugin.rs.

findings.description: insert_host_networking_resources (co-op host, 8 resources) and the resource-init block inside init_mp_game (versus/guest) are nearly identical and must be kept in sync manually. A comment on coop.rs:104 says 'keep the two in sync' — a fragile manual contract.
findings.recommendation: Extract insert_shared_mp_networking_resources(commands: &mut Commands) and call it from both. Each site then only adds its own extras (CoopGuestConnected, LocalSpellOrigin).

findings.description: PAUSE_BUTTON_STYLE is defined identically in both systems/disconnected.rs and systems/pause_menu.rs (same width/height/border/font/colors).
findings.recommendation: Move to systems/constants.rs and import in both files.

findings.description: MpSpawnQueue::pop_next calls Vec::remove(0) which is O(n) in the queue length. MP loading queues hold 100+ tasks (terrain + units + wizards).
findings.recommendation: Change tasks: Vec<MpSpawnTask> to tasks: VecDeque<MpSpawnTask> and use pop_front().

findings.description: Four host receive systems (receive_spell_hit_messages, receive_raise_corpse_messages, receive_apply_status_effect, receive_dispel_messages) resolve target_network_id to an Entity via units.iter().find_map() — O(n) over all networked units per incoming message. With 50-100 units and multiple per-frame messages this is measurable CPU waste.
findings.recommendation: Maintain a HashMap<u32, Entity> resource updated by assign_network_ids (insert on assign, remove on despawn) so all four receive systems do O(1) lookup.

findings.description: send_coop_level_over hard-codes host_spell_damage: 0.0 and host_spell_healing: 0.0 with comment 'WS9 fills these from the host's LocalWizardStats'. LocalWizardStats IS inserted for the co-op host and accumulates real data but is never read here. The guest's score silently receives zeros for the host's spell contribution.
findings.recommendation: Add Res<LocalWizardStats> to send_coop_level_over's parameters and populate the fields from local_stats. Remove the WS9 stub comment.

findings.description: Every reliable-message receive system repeats identical 8-line drain-then-re-queue boilerplate: drain to Vec, iterate, push unhandled back. 15 instances across the module. The pattern is correct but every new message type requires duplicating it.
findings.recommendation: Extract a helper drain_messages(connection, |msg| -> Option<NetworkMessage>) that drives one loop and re-queues Some(msg) returns. All 15 call sites collapse to one closure.

findings.description: Fragile Form polymorph talent reduces sheep HP via the cast-time params.sheep_hp field (not a marker component), so the ApplyStatusEffect payload cannot represent it. The host spawns a full-HP sheep when the guest casts Fragile Form polymorph. Documented in a comment as a known gap.
findings.recommendation: Add a fragile_form bit to the polymorph flags byte in status_flags, set it in forward_status_effects_to_host, and apply FRAGILE_SHEEP_HP in apply_status_to_entity. One-line protocol addition, backward-compatible.

findings.description: The two most complex dispatch functions (apply_state_snapshot and apply_status_to_entity) have no unit tests. The ghost-gating contract and material-handle ownership rules are intricate enough that future edits could silently introduce regressions.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for: (a) corpse->alive transition does not swap to a shared material handle, (b) apply_status_to_entity Polymorph with polymorph_capture=None falls through to the sleep fallback, (c) attach_crdt_health skips entities that already have CrdtHealth.

findings.description: Auto-Crystal turret placement limit is broken: the code filters existing_crystals by `!c.permanent`, but newly cast turrets set crystal.permanent = true, so the filter always returns 0 and the one-turret limit never fires.
findings.recommendation: Change filter to `.filter(|(_, c)| c.permanent)` to count existing permanent turrets. Update the comment from 'non-permanent' to 'permanent'.

findings.description: The gameplay add_systems group is not .chain()-ed. crystal_network_chain reads just_absorbed set by detect_* systems; resonance_cascade_burst reads resonance.absorptions incremented inside detect_*. Bevy serialises them via shared &mut ArcaneCrystal but order is non-deterministic, causing these talent systems to frequently observe stale values from the previous frame.
findings.recommendation: Add .chain() to the gameplay system group, or use .after() to explicitly order detect_* before crystal_network_chain and resonance_cascade_burst.

findings.description: fod_beams_processed and explosions_processed are Vec<Entity> that grow unboundedly over the crystal's 25-second lifetime. Stale dead-entity IDs are never pruned, and the .contains() lookups at hits.rs:69 and hits.rs:318 are O(n) linear scans.
findings.recommendation: Switch to HashSet<Entity> for O(1) contains(), or add a retain pass at the start of each hit-detection loop to prune IDs whose entities are gone.

findings.description: Comment says 'Count crystals placed this level (non-permanent ones)' but the spawned turret IS permanent (crystal.permanent = true). The comment is the opposite of the correct intent and contributed to the F1 filter inversion.
findings.recommendation: Correct to 'Count permanent turrets placed this level' and flip the filter as described in F1.

findings.description: Comment says 'despawn oldest if at limit' but the code uses existing_crystals.iter().next() which returns an arbitrary entity with no time_alive comparison.
findings.recommendation: Either sort by time_alive to truly despawn the oldest, or change the comment to 'despawn an arbitrary crystal at limit'.

findings.description: systems.rs carries the comment 'Re-export hub for arcane_crystal systems split (Phase 14)'. The 'Phase 14' label is a migration artifact leaking internal history into the module surface.
findings.recommendation: Drop the phase reference; update to a simple description of the file's purpose.

findings.description: The disintegrate absorption path sets hit_by_disintegrate and marks absorption but does NOT call increment_resonance() or progress.increment(), unlike every other spell absorption path. No comment explains this intentional asymmetry.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment: '// Resonance/progress not incremented: disintegrate hits every frame while channelling — would spam the counter.'

findings.description: crystal_network_chain collects crystal data as a 6-tuple where _source_range, _source_emp and the inner loop's _target_range, _target_emp, _target_spell are all underscore-prefixed and never used. Unnecessary data copying per frame.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the collected tuple to only the 4 fields actually used: (Entity, Vec3, Option<RememberedSpell>, bool).

findings.description: hits.rs at 664 LOC contains five independent hit-detection systems (fireball, disintegrate/FoD beam, meteor, magic missile, chain lightning), each ~100-130 LOC. Exceeds the 300-LOC threshold without being a single match-on-enum or registry monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into hits/mod.rs + hits/fireball.rs, hits/beam.rs, hits/meteor.rs, hits/magic_missile.rs, hits/chain_lightning.rs.

findings.description: cast_vfx.rs at 468 LOC mixes four distinct VFX concerns: cast flares + SpellSchool enum (lines 1-127), floating motes (160-249), smoke poofs (252-325), dust smoke (327-375), and aura bubbles (377-468). Exceeds the 300-LOC ceiling and violates the project's 'group by concern' rule.
findings.recommendation: Split into flares.rs (cast flare + SpellSchool enum), motes.rs (floating motes), poofs.rs (smoke poof + dust smoke), and aura_bubbles.rs. Update cast_effects/mod.rs re-exports accordingly.

findings.description: spawn_school_flare_synced encodes SpellSchool as raw u8 literals (Fire => 0, ... Transmutation => 7) with no compile-time link to SpellSchoolWire in snapshot.rs:690. Adding a new variant to either enum without mirroring the other silently routes the wrong flare color to the remote peer in multiplayer — no compile error, no runtime error.
findings.recommendation: Add #[repr(u8)] with explicit discriminants to SpellSchool and replace the manual match with `school as u8`. Or unify SpellSchool and SpellSchoolWire into a single type to eliminate the dual-enum maintenance burden.

findings.description: PlagueSmoke.spawn_y doubles as a boolean sentinel: spawn_y > 0.0 means 'this is a fire puff'. A fire puff legitimately spawned at world-y=0 (e.g. flat terrain) silently loses all height-based billowing animation with no error. The doc comment at line 83 acknowledges the hack.
findings.recommendation: Add an is_fire: bool field to PlagueSmoke, or a zero-cost FirePuffMarker component so update_plague_smoke can use Has<FirePuffMarker> instead of the y-sentinel.

findings.description: spawn_fire_smoke_puff (lines 14-45) and spawn_fire_particle_puff (lines 50-79) are nearly identical. The only difference is the material argument: spawn_fire_particle_puff hardcodes assets.fire_particle.clone(). This is ~35 lines of duplication.
findings.recommendation: Remove spawn_fire_particle_puff. Its three call sites should call spawn_fire_smoke_puff passing assets.fire_particle.clone() as the material argument.

findings.description: Two gravity values are inlined as literals: 200.0 for explosion sparks (fire_effects.rs:246) and 150.0 for cast-flare sparks (cast_effects/cast_vfx.rs:55). Every other per-particle tuning value lives in constants.rs. These are the only exceptions.
findings.recommendation: Add pub(crate) const SPARK_GRAVITY: f32 = 200.0 and pub(crate) const CAST_FLARE_SPARK_GRAVITY: f32 = 150.0 to constants.rs and reference them at the spawn sites.

findings.description: spawn_fire_black_smoke (line 82), spawn_fire_rising_smoke (line 116), and spawn_heat_shimmer_sized (heat_shimmer.rs:27) are declared pub but are only called within the vfx module. They are not re-exported in area_effects/mod.rs, yet their pub visibility makes them accessible anywhere in the crate.
findings.recommendation: Change visibility to pub(super) (or pub(crate) if future cross-module use is planned) to match project conventions and narrow the public API surface.

findings.description: update_fire_particle_time and update_aura_sphere_time both call Assets::iter_mut() every frame (under is_spell_effects_active) regardless of whether any relevant particle entities are alive. The outer guard prevents menu-state waste but not in-game waste when no fire or aura effects are active.
findings.recommendation: Guard update_fire_particle_time with any_exist::<FireOrangeSmokePuff>() and update_aura_sphere_time with any_exist::<AuraBubbleVfx>() to skip the material iteration when no relevant entities exist.

findings.description: The beam-origin / range-clamped-target / direction / length computation is copy-pasted verbatim between the Channeling arm (lines 74-100) and the Casting arm (lines 118-140). The blocks are byte-for-byte identical except for the BeamAction variant returned.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn compute_beam_geometry(wizard_pos: Vec3, target_pos: Vec3, spell_range: f32) -> (Vec3, Vec3, f32) returning (origin, direction, length) and call it from both arms.

findings.description: The perpendicular-basis construction (up fallback + right = direction.cross(up).normalize() + forward = right.cross(direction).normalize()) is duplicated between emit_impact_particles (lines 62-68) and emit_beam_smoke (lines 164-170) in the same file.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn beam_perp_basis(direction: Vec3) -> (Vec3, Vec3) at the bottom of particles.rs and call it from both functions.

findings.description: intersects_hitbox_cylinder accepts _hitbox_height: f32 (leading underscore = intentionally unused). The body does not cull units whose vertical extent falls outside the beam's Y range. Callers believe height is factored in, but it is not.
findings.recommendation: Either add a vertical extent check using hitbox_height, or remove the parameter from the signature and all call-sites so the contract matches the implementation.

findings.description: The doc comment on contains_point_with_radius states 'The beam has uniform width along its entire length,' but line 247 implements a cone that widens from 0 at the origin to full width at the tip. The sibling method intersects_hitbox_cylinder correctly documents 'Cone radius widens linearly.'
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc comment to say 'cone that widens from 0 at the origin to full width at the tip.'

findings.description: The pseudo-random angle for annihilation resonance mini-fireballs uses beam.resonance_timer * 137.5. After resonance_timer -= MINI_FIREBALL_INTERVAL the timer resets to near-zero (~0..0.016 s), so the angle barely advances from 0 each interval — fireballs cluster in a narrow arc rather than spreading around the full circle as the comment implies.
findings.recommendation: Replace with time.elapsed_secs() * 137.5 so each pulse fires at a meaningfully different angle, matching the rotating-spread approach used in emit_impact_particles.

findings.description: update_beam_eclipse falls back to the magic literal 500.0 for spell_range when no Wizard entity is found. This unnamed magic number has no explanation in context.
findings.recommendation: Define constants::FALLBACK_SPELL_RANGE: f32 = 500.0 with a doc comment, or gate the system on any_with_component::<Wizard>() to avoid the fallback entirely.

findings.description: The tier-3 option 2 talent is called 'resonance' in TalentConfig and all constant names (MINI_FIREBALL_INTERVAL etc.), but the constant section header in constants.rs says '// Talent: Beam Fireballs (T3-2)' while the comment in talent_config.rs says '// Unstable Resonance'. Two different names for the same talent exist in-source.
findings.recommendation: Standardise: rename TalentConfig::resonance bool to beam_fireballs and align the comment in talent_config.rs with the player-visible name 'Beam Fireballs'.

findings.description: The pure-math geometry methods (contains_point_with_radius, intersects_hitbox_cylinder, eclipse_geometry) implement non-trivial spatial math: cone projections, XZ flattening, ellipse clipping. No unit tests exist. These are the highest-churn collision primitives in the spell.
findings.recommendation: Add #[cfg(test)] unit tests covering: point at origin (should miss), point at tip (should hit), lateral miss, ground_collision XZ flattening, cone growth at t=0.5, eclipse_geometry range-clipping.

findings.description: apply_finger_of_death_damage targets query is Without<Wizard> only — no Without<GhostEntity>. On the guest peer, the beam can mutate Health on host ghost units (which carry a real Health component via CRDT), causing local-only HP divergence. Additionally, DeathmarkDebuff is inserted on ghost units (line 217), which can trigger spurious chain beams when the ghost's CRDT-replicated HP transitions to ≤0 locally.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to the targets query filter-tuple, matching the pattern in entangle/casting/root_effects.rs:66 with its explanatory comment.

findings.description: update_reapers_scythe targets query (Without<Wizard>) has no Without<GhostEntity>. The per-frame sweep damage loop runs for the full 1-second sweep duration and can mutate guest ghost unit Health on every tick, causing HP divergence from host-authoritative CRDT state.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to the targets query in update_reapers_scythe.

findings.description: apply_necrotic_explosion_damage targets query (Without<Wizard>) has no Without<GhostEntity>. Every NecroticExplosionBurst applies AoE damage on its first tick to all non-Wizard entities in radius, which includes ghost units with Health components.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to the targets query in apply_necrotic_explosion_damage.

findings.description: update_deathmark_debuffs all_enemies query (Without<Wizard>) has no Without<GhostEntity>. A ghost unit implanted with DeathmarkDebuff (via the unfixed F1 path) will trigger chain-beam emission when its locally-visible HP reaches ≤0, causing a spurious beam that then passes through the ungated damage system. Prerequisite: fix the targets query in apply_finger_of_death_damage (F1) to prevent debuff insertion on ghosts.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to both the marked_targets and all_enemies queries in update_deathmark_debuffs.

findings.description: The 8-line block computing beam_origin, range-clamped target, direction, and beam_length is copy-pasted verbatim inside the CastingState::Casting branch (line 267) and the CastingState::Resting first-spawn branch (line 325). Any tuning change must be made in two places.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private fn compute_beam_direction_and_length(cursor_pos: Vec3, beam_origin: Vec3, spell_range: f32, max_len: f32) -> (Vec3, f32) and call it from both branches.

findings.description: The doc comment on process_pending_undead_raises reads '/// Computes talent-modified parameters for Finger of Death.' — a copy-paste error from compute_fod_params in casting_logic.rs. The function actually raises killed units as undead.
findings.recommendation: Replace with '/// Raises killed units as undead when PendingUndeadRaise is present (deferred by one frame so corpses exist).'

findings.description: process_pending_undead_raises takes Option<Res<PendingUndeadRaise>> despite the plugin gating it with resource_exists::<PendingUndeadRaise>. The inner Option-unwrap guard is always Some, making the Option redundant and misleading to readers.
findings.recommendation: Change the parameter to Res<PendingUndeadRaise> and remove the let Some(pending) = pending else { return; } guard.

findings.description: Five materials.get(&handle).cloned().unwrap_or_default() calls across damage.rs (lines 38, 339, 364), necrotic_explosion.rs (line 29), and beam_effects.rs (line 224) silently substitute a blank StandardMaterial if the asset hasn't loaded yet. Invisible geometry is produced with no log output, making asset-load-order races invisible.
findings.recommendation: Replace with .unwrap_or_else(|| { warn!("FoD: material asset not ready"); StandardMaterial::default() }) so asset-loading races surface in the log.

findings.description: damage.rs is 385 LOC and mixes two distinct concerns: spawn_beam (mesh/material factory, lines 27–69) and apply_finger_of_death_damage (beam hit-scan, wall/rock occlusion, all talent post-effects, audio, VFX, mana drain, vein particle spawn — lines 71–385). The factory is independently readable and testable.
findings.recommendation: Extract spawn_beam into casting/spawn.rs and update casting/mod.rs to re-export it from there.

findings.description: The second-phase teleport completion logic is duplicated verbatim between the early-release path (lines 132–205) and the timer-complete path (lines 237–298). Both paths call execute_teleport, populate the same result fields, and handle Lingering Gate — ~60 lines of near-identical code each. The only real difference is that early release uses spawn_aura_bubble_contracting_synced for the source bubble while timer-complete uses spawn_aura_bubble_synced.
findings.recommendation: Extract a fn complete_second_phase(…, contracting: bool) helper in finalize.rs that takes source/dest positions, radius, and the contraction flag, and call it from both sites.

findings.description: The timer-complete Phase 2 path calls mana.consume(effective_mana_cost) without re-checking can_afford. The guard at line 230 only runs when entering CastingState::Resting; if mana is drained between pressing and cast completion the game over-consumes into negative values. The early-release path (line 145) correctly re-checks can_afford before consuming.
findings.recommendation: Add if !mana.can_afford(effective_mana_cost) { casting_state.cancel(); return result; } before line 248, matching the early-release guard.

findings.description: cleanup.rs is misnamed: it contains apply_post_teleport_effects (post-cast talent application) and update_circle_animations (animation tick), neither of which are cleanup. Only cleanup_teleport_on_spell_switch belongs in a file called cleanup.rs. The wrong file name misleads navigation.
findings.recommendation: Rename cleanup.rs to post_effects.rs (housing apply_post_teleport_effects + update_circle_animations). Move cleanup_teleport_on_spell_switch to a short cleanup.rs or inline into cast_input.rs.

findings.description: TeleportDestinationCircle::pulse_scale and TeleportSourceCircle::pulse_scale (lines 60–64 and 89–93) are byte-for-byte identical — same formula, same inline magic numbers pulse_freq = 2.0 and pulse_amplitude = 0.05.
findings.recommendation: Extract a free function fn pulse_scale(time_alive: f32) -> f32 in components.rs and delegate both impl blocks to it. Promote the two magic numbers to named constants in constants.rs.

findings.description: Constant docs say 'stun enemies on arrival' (line 42) and 'attack speed bonus for allies on arrival' (line 44), but arrival/cleanup.rs:24–33 applies both Stunned and DisorientingHaste to ALL teleported entities regardless of team.
findings.recommendation: Clarify design intent: if all-entities is correct (consistent with friendly-fire philosophy), update constant docs to say 'all teleported units.' If selective stun is the target, add team-based filtering in apply_post_teleport_effects.

findings.description: LingeringGateMarker and DimensionalRift manually decrement time_remaining in their own systems, while DisorientingHaste and RiftCooldown (same module) correctly implement TimedModifier and use the shared update_timed_modifier generic. Two patterns for the same job in the same module.
findings.recommendation: Implement TimedModifier for LingeringGateMarker; the rift expiry side-effect (resetting TeleportCaster) can remain in tick_lingering_gate with a check. Add a comment for DimensionalRift explaining why it diverges if kept manual.

findings.description: _primed_spell: &PrimedSpell is passed to teleport_casting_logic but is never read (underscore-suppressed). Empowerment is accessed from source_circle.empowerment instead.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead parameter from the function signature.

findings.description: The module-level doc comment reads 'Re-export hub for teleport systems split (Phase 14)'. Phase 14 is a stale internal refactoring ticket reference with no meaning to a future reader.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a plain description, e.g. '//! Re-export hub: arrival and casting system functions.'

findings.description: update_ice_explosions iterates ALL IceExplosion entities with no Without<GhostSpellEffect> guard on the explosions query. Ghost IceExplosion entities on the co-op guest have damage=0.0 so health is unaffected, but apply_frost_accumulation is called with the full frost_per_hit (0.3 or 0.6 with Permafrost). This double-applies frost status on the guest, causing incorrect slow and freeze buildup.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostSpellEffect> to the explosions query in update_ice_explosions. Ghost explosions handle only visuals; the gameplay damage path must be host-authoritative only.

findings.description: ABSOLUTE_ZERO_SLOW_PER_FRAME is added once per frame regardless of frame duration (no * delta). At 30 FPS the slow stacks at half the rate of 60 FPS. Other per-second quantities in the same function (ABSOLUTE_ZERO_MANA_PER_SEC * delta, ABSOLUTE_ZERO_DPS * delta) are correctly delta-scaled.
findings.recommendation: Rename to ABSOLUTE_ZERO_SLOW_PER_SEC and multiply by delta at the call site: az.accumulated_slow -= ABSOLUTE_ZERO_SLOW_PER_SEC * delta. Adjust constant value to preserve feel at 60 FPS (0.005 * 60 = 0.3/s).

findings.description: shards.rs is 871 lines — nearly 3x the project's 300-line threshold. It contains at least four independent concerns: projectile spawn/physics/collision (~245 LOC), explosion update + damage (~165 LOC), talent gameplay systems (Sleet Storm, Absolute Zero, Blizzard, Ice Age / ~300 LOC), and snow VFX (~100 LOC). Not a match/registry monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into: projectile.rs (spawn, physics, collision, spawn_ice_explosion), explosion.rs (update_ice_explosions), talents.rs (apply_sleet_storm_evasion, update_absolute_zero, decay_absolute_zero_slow, end_absolute_zero_on_release, update_blizzard_position, update_frozen_ground, spawn_frozen_ground_patch), snow.rs (spawn_snow_particles, update_snow_particles, update_storm_ring).

findings.description: The sfx_scale computation and audio::play_impact_sfx_scaled call are copy-pasted identically in all three collision branches (wall at line 158, rock at line 190, ground at line 230) inside check_ice_projectile_collisions.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private fn play_squall_impact_sfx(commands, sfx, game_config, pos, is_hailstone) helper called from all three branches.

findings.description: IceProjectile has #[allow(dead_code)] at struct level and on the damage_type field (line 100). The damage_type is always DamageType::Frost (hardcoded in constructor) and is never read by any system. Dead field silently suppresses a compiler warning that reveals unused code.
findings.recommendation: Remove the damage_type field from IceProjectile and drop both #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions. Hard-code DamageType::Frost directly where IceExplosion is spawned.

findings.description: The doc-comment on spawn_ice_projectiles reads 'Applies or inserts a [SlowMovementModifier] on an entity.' — verbatim copy-paste from the apply_or_insert_slow helper above it. The function actually spawns ice projectiles.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Spawns ice projectiles into the storm area on a timed interval.'

findings.description: FROST_PER_HIT * delta * 5.0 uses an unexplained magic multiplier 5.0 for the Absolute Zero continuous frost accumulation rate. Its intended meaning (e.g. 5 hits/sec equivalent) is opaque and not covered by any constant.
findings.recommendation: Extract to ABSOLUTE_ZERO_FROST_RATE_MULT: f32 = 5.0 in constants.rs with a doc comment explaining the equivalence.

findings.description: systems.rs carries the comment 'Re-export hub for squall systems split (Phase 14).' — the 'Phase 14' label is stale development scaffolding with no value for readers.
findings.recommendation: Replace with 'Re-export hub for squall systems.'

findings.description: use rand::Rng; is re-imported inside the body of update_ice_explosions at line 337, even though it is already present at the top-level imports (line 5). The inner use is redundant.
findings.recommendation: Remove the inner use rand::Rng; at line 337.

findings.description: let interval = SNOW_SPAWN_INTERVAL; is a trivial rename of the constant used exactly once, adding an indirection layer with no value.
findings.recommendation: Use SNOW_SPAWN_INTERVAL directly in the subsequent division expressions.

findings.description: When quick_foundations places two wall segments, result.obstacle_bounds is overwritten each loop iteration so only the last segment's bounds are returned to the caller. handle_wall_of_stone_casting then sends a single WallPlaced network message with only those bounds; the guest's pathfinding grid ends up with only one of the two segments registered as a blocked obstacle.
findings.recommendation: Send one WallPlaced message per segment inside the loop (or accumulate both into a Vec), matching what the local ObstacleChanged path already does for each segment.

findings.description: At 332 lines, components.rs mixes three distinct concerns: (1) the WallOfStone OBB geometry struct with six non-trivial geometry methods; (2) caster/preview state types (WallOfStoneCaster, WallOfStonePreview); (3) all talent and status components plus the PermafrostAuraTimer resource. Exceeds the 300-line guideline with mixed concerns.
findings.recommendation: Split into wall.rs (WallOfStone struct and OBB methods), caster.rs (WallOfStoneCaster, WallOfStonePreview), and talent_components.rs (talent params, WallTalents, LivingStoneTracker, PermafrostAuraTimer, WallRising, CollapseExploded, DispelledWall, WallHealth alias).

findings.description: The doc comment on handle_wall_of_stone_cancel reads 'Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.' — a stale copy-paste from casting/talents.rs. The function actually cancels an in-progress wall drag and despawns the preview entity.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment describing the cancel behavior.

findings.description: maze_architect_bonus does two full wall-query passes every frame — first to count walls and detect the talent, then to adjust HP. It has no change-detection guard: it runs even when wall state has not changed, iterating all walls twice per frame regardless.
findings.recommendation: Collapse into one pass and add a Local<(usize, bool)> tracking last (wall_count, bonus_active) to short-circuit frames where nothing has changed.

findings.description: File holds five unrelated concerns at 389 LOC: projectile physics (update_meteor_projectiles), an enemy-search helper (find_nearest_non_defender_xz), smoke-trail VFX (spawn_meteor_smoke_trail), ground-collision/damage/pathfinding (check_meteor_collisions), and Extinction Event logic (process_extinction_event). Exceeds the 300-line threshold and is not a single match/registry monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into meteor/movement.rs (physics + find_nearest helper), meteor/trail.rs (smoke/glow VFX), and meteor/collision.rs (collision + pathfinding write + extinction event).

findings.description: File contains two distinct concerns at 343 LOC: talent-config resolution (MeteorTalentConfig struct + compute_meteor_talent_config, ~125 LOC) and the casting state machine (handle_meteor_fall_casting + meteor_fall_casting_logic, ~218 LOC).
findings.recommendation: Extract MeteorTalentConfig and compute_meteor_talent_config to a sibling casting/talents.rs, leaving input_casting.rs purely for casting input handling.

findings.description: Three different idioms for XZ-plane distance within the same module: (dx*dx + dz*dz).sqrt() at projectile.rs:230 and 264, Vec3::new(..., 0.0, ...).length() at ground_fire.rs:88, and the shared xz_distance() helper from spells::utils at explosion.rs:94.
findings.recommendation: Normalise all four call sites to use the existing xz_distance() helper from spells::utils::spell_math.

findings.description: MeteorTalentConfig (private) and MeteorProjectileTalentFlags (pub(crate), projectile_spawn.rs:16) are parallel structs with seven overlapping fields (aftershock, volcanic_eruption, ground_fire_*_mult, tracking, is_extinction). Talent values are manually transcribed config -> storm -> projectile at two separate call sites with no compile-time enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Unify to a single MeteorTalentParams type, or add From<&MeteorTalentConfig> for MeteorProjectileTalentFlags, so adding a new talent field only requires one edit.

findings.description: Ten manual field assignments from MeteorTalentConfig into MeteorFallStorm (lines 290-300). If a new talent field is added to the config struct it must also be added to this copy block with no compile-time enforcement of completeness.
findings.recommendation: Add an apply_talents(&mut self, cfg: &MeteorTalentConfig) method to MeteorFallStorm, or resolve via the type consolidation suggested in finding F04.

findings.description: When tracking bias is active, the spawn bundle's Transform is immediately overwritten by a second deferred commands.entity(entity).insert(Transform{...}). The spawn-bundle Transform is wasted and a future refactor could silently drop the override without a compile error.
findings.recommendation: Compute the biased spawn position before calling spawn_meteor_projectile_entity and pass the final position directly, eliminating the post-spawn override.

findings.description: Module-doc reads 'Re-export hub for meteor_fall systems split (Phase 14).' — the internal refactor phase number is a stale artefact with no reader value.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a plain description: 'Re-export hub for meteor_fall sub-module symbols.'

findings.description: check_grease_ignition queries GreaseZone without Without<GhostSpellEffect>. Ghost grease zones are full GreaseZone entities on the guest. Fire-source queries (fireball_explosions at line 41, wall_of_fires at line 43, etc.) also lack Without<GhostSpellEffect>, so a ghost fireball explosion can trigger ignition on a ghost zone. Once ignited, apply_grease_burn runs on that ghost zone with no Without<GhostEntity> guard on targets (line 269), causing duplicate burn damage to real units.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to the zones query. Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to all six fire-source queries in check_grease_ignition.

findings.description: apply_grease_burn queries GreaseZone without Without<GhostSpellEffect>. On the guest, this processes ghost zones and the targets query (line 269) has no Without<GhostEntity> filter, causing duplicate burn damage to real units from ghost zones triggered by ghost fire sources.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to the zone query and Without<GhostEntity> to the targets query in apply_grease_burn.

findings.description: apply_grease_slow queries GreaseZone without Without<GhostSpellEffect>. On the guest this increments ghost zone time_alive (enabling cleanup_grease_zone to despawn ghosts prematurely), and runs Slip and Fall stun and Oil Slick vulnerability paths on units near ghost zones. Targets query (line 34) also lacks Without<GhostEntity>.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to the zone query and Without<GhostEntity> to the targets query in apply_grease_slow.

findings.description: cleanup_grease_zone calls try_despawn on GreaseZone entities when time_alive >= duration, with no Without<GhostSpellEffect> filter. Ghost zone time_alive is incremented locally (via apply_grease_slow), so the guest will despawn ghost zones on its local clock, out of sync with the host snapshot managed by ghost_spawn.rs.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to cleanup_grease_zone's zone query. Ghost zone lifecycle is already managed by ghost_spawn.rs when the host removes them from the snapshot.

findings.description: update_grease_regeneration and cleanup_grease_debuffs (line 136) lack Without<GhostSpellEffect> on their zone queries. Regeneration on ghost zones would reset time_alive and remove GreaseIgnited on the guest, corrupting ghost visual state.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to both zone queries in update_grease_regeneration and cleanup_grease_debuffs.

findings.description: burn.rs is 325 lines mixing three distinct concerns: ignition detection (check_grease_ignition, ~218 lines scanning 6 fire-source types with talent burst logic), fire-spread timing (update_grease_fire_spread), and burn-tick damage (apply_grease_burn). Per project convention files over 300 lines that are not a single match-on-enum or asset registry must be split.
findings.recommendation: Extract check_grease_ignition into ignite/detection.rs. Keep update_grease_fire_spread and apply_grease_burn in burn.rs.

findings.description: The doc comment '/// Helper to write an obstacle event for a grease zone.' on check_grease_ignition is a stale copy-paste from write_grease_obstacle in casting/obstacle.rs. check_grease_ignition scans fire sources, inserts GreaseIgnited, applies burst damage, and handles Geyser/Lingering Flames talents.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment describing the function's actual purpose.

findings.description: check_grease_ignition allocates a Vec<(Vec3, f32)> via .collect() every frame for ignited_zones, even when there are no non-ignited zones to check against. The system is gated any_exist::<GreaseIgnited>() but the collection happens unconditionally before the outer loop.
findings.recommendation: Scan ignited_zone_query inline inside the outer loop to eliminate the per-frame heap allocation, or gate the collection behind an early return if zones (non-ignited) is empty.

findings.description: fade_grease_zone calls materials.get_mut(material_handle) every frame for every active zone — even during the non-fading period (fade == 1.0, emissive constant). Bevy marks the material dirty on every get_mut call, forcing GPU re-upload each frame.
findings.recommendation: Guard the base_color write with if fade < 1.0. Accept the per-frame iridescent sheen update as intentional but avoid the redundant alpha/base_color mutation during the non-fading window.

findings.description: GreaseOilSlickDebuff::new() and GreaseRegenerating::new() (line 173) are zero-argument constructors with trivial bodies. Rust convention for such types is #[derive(Default)]; clippy::new_without_default would flag these.
findings.recommendation: Add #[derive(Default)] to both structs and replace new() call sites with ::default().

findings.description: systems.rs is a pure wildcard re-export hub (pub use super::casting::*; pub use super::ignite::*;). Any new pub fn added to casting/ or ignite/ automatically enters the systems namespace without explicit review. Other spell modules use explicit named re-exports in their sub-package mod.rs files.
findings.recommendation: Switch to explicit named re-exports, or add a comment documenting that all public items from both sub-packages are intentionally surfaced through this hub.

findings.description: forward_dispel_impacts_to_host queries spell_effects with &NetworkedSpellEffect, but ghost spell effects on the guest carry GhostSpellEffect + NetworkEntityId only — they never receive NetworkedSpellEffect. The query returns zero results on the guest, so guest-cast Dispel never forwards to the host and never suppresses any of the host's persistent spell effects.
findings.recommendation: Add NetworkedSpellEffect { kind } to ghost spell effects when spawning them in guest_visuals/ghost_effect_spawn.rs, or change the forwarding query to join on NetworkEntityId + GhostSpellEffect directly. Either path must match how the host validates dispellability in receive_dispel_messages.

findings.description: collect_dispellable_effects allocates a fresh Vec<_> inside the per-impact loop (and again inside the NullZone loop at line 408), rebuilding it every frame for every active impact/zone by iterating all networked spell effects each time.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the Vec allocation and collection outside the respective iteration loops — collect once before 'for … in &mut impacts' and before 'for … in &mut zones', then pass &all_dispellable as a slice.

findings.description: bolt.rs is 872 LOC mixing five distinct concerns: update_dispel_impacts (gameplay), update_null_zones (gameplay), tick_ghost_dispel_impacts (MP visual), forward_dispel_impacts_to_host (MP network), and six shared helpers (suppress_spell_effects_in_radius, collect_dispellable_effects, remove_mind_control_in_radius, strip_spell_shields_in_radius, spell_edge_distance, despawn_spell_effect). The project convention caps non-cohesive files at ~300 LOC.
findings.recommendation: Split into impacts.rs (update_dispel_impacts + update_null_zones), multiplayer.rs (tick_ghost_dispel_impacts + forward_dispel_impacts_to_host + DispelForwarded), and suppress.rs (the six shared helpers). The glob re-export in systems.rs continues to work with no downstream breakage.

findings.description: NullZone alpha fade uses life_frac = time_remaining / constants::NULL_ZONE_DURATION, but time_remaining is initialized to NULL_ZONE_DURATION * scorched_mult (line 348). With Scorched Earth active (mult=3.0) the zone starts at 30s but the denominator is fixed at 10s, giving life_frac=3.0 and an alpha of 0.45 — 3x the intended max of 0.15. The zone appears over-bright for the first 20 of its 30 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Add a total_duration: f32 field to NullZone, set it at spawn time to NULL_ZONE_DURATION * scorched_mult, and compute life_frac = time_remaining / zone.total_duration.

findings.description: Petrified is referenced via full inline crate path (crate::game::units::components::Petrified) in both the query tuple (line 81) and the removal call (line 287), while all other units::components types are cleanly imported at the top of the file.
findings.recommendation: Add Petrified to the existing 'use crate::game::units::components::{…}' import block.

findings.description: systems.rs is a glob re-export hub (pub use super::bolt::*; pub use super::casting::*) left over from Phase 14. External callers in dispeller/ import via systems::, but host_systems/dispel_receive.rs imports directly from bolt::, creating two inconsistent access paths to the same symbols.
findings.recommendation: Decide on one canonical access path. Either remove systems.rs and have all callers import from bolt/casting directly, or enforce that all external callers go through systems:: and fix the direct bolt:: access in dispel_receive.rs.

findings.description: update_null_zones uses is_gameplay_running while every other system in the plugin uses is_spell_effects_active. The asymmetry is correct but unexplained; a future maintainer may 'fix' it.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment: '// NullZone is host-only gameplay simulation, not a guest visual — use is_gameplay_running, not is_spell_effects_active'.

findings.description: Fireball::damage_type is suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)] and never read. The explosion spawn always passes constants::DAMAGE_TYPE directly, so the field is written at construction but has zero downstream effect. Silent divergence if someone modifies the field expecting it to change explosion damage type.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field and the allow-attribute, or pass fireball.damage_type into spawn_explosion_with_talents so the field is honoured.

findings.description: Doc comment on move_fireballs reads 'Local wizard fireball casting - reads mouse input' - copy-pasted from casting.rs. The function only integrates velocity; it reads no input.
findings.recommendation: Fix to 'Advances fireball positions by their velocity each frame.'

findings.description: missile.rs is 434 lines containing two unrelated systems: move_magic_missiles (guided steering + homing, ~190 LOC) and check_magic_missile_collisions (obstacle + unit hit detection + damage + seeker-swarm split, ~180 LOC), plus a private spawn helper. Project convention requires splitting files >300 LOC that are not a single cohesive concern.
findings.recommendation: Split into movement.rs (move_magic_missiles + despawn_distant_magic_missiles) and collision.rs (check_magic_missile_collisions + spawn_missile_detonation).

findings.description: partial_cmp(...).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal) in the closest-enemy fallback. Project convention forbids .unwrap() in production; .unwrap_or on float comparison is the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Replace with .total_cmp() which is NaN-safe and requires no unwrap_or.

findings.description: _time_secs: f32 parameter is unused (leading underscore) in spawn_explosion_with_talents. Dead parameter adds noise to every call site.
findings.recommendation: Remove the parameter and update all call sites.

findings.description: preview_height = 10.0 is a local let repeated 3 times in spell_casting.rs and once in placement.rs::wall_transform. If the wall render height changes, all four sites must be updated in sync.
findings.recommendation: Extract pub(super) const WALL_RENDER_HEIGHT: f32 = 10.0 in constants.rs and reference it at all four sites.

findings.description: Two different 'scorched earth' effects share near-identical names: ScorchedEarthFire (fireball talent - persistent burning ground) and ScorchedEarthZone (wall-of-fire talent - slow debuff zone). They appear adjacently in dispel/bolt.rs and the similar names already caused comment drift there.
findings.recommendation: Rename ScorchedEarthFire to FireballGroundFire or NapalmGroundFire to make the owning spell explicit. Update all import sites.

findings.description: Two sites (explosion_lifecycle.rs:248 and trail_effects.rs:74) call sphere_materials.get(...).expect('sphere material template').clone() but explosion_spawn.rs:45 already uses the shared clone_sphere_material() helper for the same operation. Inconsistent usage of available shared helper.
findings.recommendation: Replace both raw .get(...).expect(...).clone() calls with clone_sphere_material(sphere_materials, &visual_assets.fireball_explosion_sphere).

findings.description: Wall/rock/tree obstacle-collision is a copy-paste loop across at least three spell modules: fireball (movement.rs:65-100), magic missile (missile.rs:241-280), and squall shards. Each independently iterates walls (contains_point_xz), rocks (blocks_projectile), and optionally trees. Any new terrain obstacle type requires changes in every spell collision system.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn check_terrain_obstacle_hit(pos, walls, rocks, trees) -> bool into spells/utils.rs and call it from all three collision systems.

findings.description: apply_wall_of_fire_damage and cleanup_wall_of_fire have no Without<GhostSpellEffect> filter. On the guest client, host walls are replicated as WallOfFireEffect with GhostSpellEffect and start=ZERO, end=ZERO, damage_per_tick=0.0. The zero-damage sentinel mitigates HP damage but: (a) time_alive advances via local delta racing CRDT; (b) TerrainDamageMessage fires with position Vec3::ZERO; (c) InsideWallOfFire and FirestormMarked can be inserted on local units near origin; (d) cleanup_wall_of_fire despawns ghost walls via local timer, potentially racing snapshot reconciliation and emitting spurious ObstacleChanged::Removed.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to both apply_wall_of_fire_damage and cleanup_wall_of_fire queries, mirroring apply_explosion_damage/cleanup_finished_explosions in the fireball module.

findings.description: spawn_explosion_bubbles has no Without<GhostSpellEffect> filter. Ghost fireball explosions on the guest have ExplosionBubbleSpawner. When triggered, sub-bubbles are spawned with OnGameplayScreen (line 270) instead of OnMultiplayerGameScreen, so they leak and are not cleaned up when the multiplayer game screen is torn down.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostSpellEffect> to the spawners query, or propagate the correct screen-lifetime marker from the parent explosion entity (the spawn_fireball_visuals generic M: Component + Clone pattern shows how).

findings.description: `let _t = time.elapsed_secs();` is fetched but never used in `handle_undead_detonation`. Dead code left from an earlier draft.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `let _t = ...` line.

findings.description: The comment on `apply_black_hole_damage` states the system is 'gated to the host in MP (it lives under MovementCalculationSet via the plugin's chain).' In the plugin, only `apply_gravitational_forces` and `apply_corpse_gravity_and_despawn` are added to MovementCalculationSet; `apply_black_hole_damage` is not. The system runs on both peers via `is_spell_effects_active`. The premise of the ghost-filter justification is factually wrong.
findings.recommendation: Correct the comment: the system runs on both peers; it is intentionally unfiltered because Health is CRDT-merged and damage is idempotent per peer. Remove the false MovementCalculationSet claim.

findings.description: `fn horizontal_distance` is defined twice with identical bodies in `cloud/spawn.rs` and `cloud/damage.rs`. The shared utility `xz_distance` already exists at `spells/utils/spell_math.rs` and is used by `spike_growth`.
findings.recommendation: Remove both local definitions and use `crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils::xz_distance` in both files.

findings.description: `spawn_pandemic_clouds` runs on both peers (`is_spell_effects_active`) and its `clouds` query has no `Without<GhostSpellEffect>` filter. In MP the guest holds ghost copies of host-cast clouds. When a unit dies near a ghost cloud, the guest spuriously spawns a local authoritative child cloud, firing `ObstacleChanged` events and dealing damage from the wrong peer.
findings.recommendation: Add `Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostSpellEffect>` to the `clouds` query, mirroring `move_plague_wind_cloud` and `apply_plague_wind_damage`.

findings.description: `apply_spike_growth_damage` runs on both peers (`is_spell_effects_active`) and its `zones` query has no `Without<GhostSpellEffect>` filter. In MP the guest has ghost copies of all host-cast `SpikeGrowthZone` entities. The guest applies zone damage, inserts `ZonePresenceTracker`/`SpikeGrowthLingeringPoison` on ghost units, and emits spurious talent progress increments from the wrong peer.
findings.recommendation: Add `Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostSpellEffect>` to the `zones` query, matching `apply_plague_wind_damage`.

findings.description: `spike_storm_volley` runs on both peers and queries `zones` without a `GhostSpellEffect` filter. On the guest, every ghost zone with `spike_storm = true` periodically spawns local `SpikeStormProjectile` entities (not networked) that deal redundant damage to ghost units via `update_spike_storm_projectiles`.
findings.recommendation: Add `Without<GhostSpellEffect>` to the `zones` query in `spike_storm_volley`; also consider gating `update_spike_storm_projectiles` to `is_gameplay_running` if Spike Storm projectiles are intentionally not networked.

findings.description: `plague_wind/casting.rs` is 392 lines, exceeding the 300-line limit. It bundles the outer system, the inner `plague_wind_casting_logic` state machine, `arrow_transform`, and the `cleanup_indicator` helper.
findings.recommendation: Split into `casting.rs` (outer system + casting logic, ~230 lines) and `indicator.rs` (`arrow_transform` + `cleanup_indicator`).

findings.description: `input_casting.rs` is 340 lines, over the 300-line limit. Contains `compute_talent_params`, the outer system, and a 140-line `raise_the_dead_casting_logic` inner function.
findings.recommendation: Move `raise_the_dead_casting_logic` to the existing `raising.rs`; keep `input_casting.rs` as the thin outer system + `compute_talent_params`.

findings.description: `black_hole/casting.rs` is 328 lines, just over the limit. Contains `compute_talent_params`, `spawn_black_hole`, the outer casting system, and `black_hole_casting_logic`.
findings.recommendation: Move `compute_talent_params` and `black_hole_casting_logic` to a new `casting_logic.rs`; keep `spawn_black_hole` and the outer system in `casting.rs`.

findings.description: `TWIN_STARS_MANA_MULT = 1.0` is a no-op constant (multiplying by 1.0 is identical to the base branch of 1.0). Both code paths in the casting system produce the same result.
findings.recommendation: Either set this to a non-trivial multiplier if Twin Stars should cost more mana, or remove the constant and the `mana_mult` indirection entirely.

findings.description: Both `handle_perpetual_unrest` (line 243) and `tick_revenant_raise` (line 295) call `compute_talent_params(active_talents.as_deref())` every frame they execute, reconstructing the talent param struct from scratch via `ActiveTalents` lookups for persistent ambient effects.
findings.recommendation: Store `talent_params` on the `PerpetualUnrest` and `RevenantLord` components at insert time, same pattern as `SpikeGrowthTalentParams` embedded in `SpikeGrowthZone`.

findings.description: `find_nearest_corpse` computes `target_pos.distance(a.1.translation)` twice per candidate — once in the `filter` closure and again inside `min_by`. Distance is calculated for every candidate twice.
findings.recommendation: Use `filter_map` to compute distance once and store `(entity, translation, dist)`, then `min_by` on the cached distance.

findings.description: process_chain_lightning_bounces queries enemies without Without<GhostEntity>. In multiplayer the guest ghost army receives arc damage from chain lightning bounces on the host, corrupting ghost simulation state.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to the enemies query filter at line 44. Mirror the pattern already used in healing_plume/casting.rs:298.

findings.description: enemies_query and health_query in handle_chain_lightning_casting and chain_lightning_casting_logic lack Without<GhostEntity>. The initial damage hit on cast can strike ghost units.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to enemies_query (line 54) and to the health_query (lines 57-61).

findings.description: ArcTargetFilter type alias excludes LightningStrike entities but not GhostEntity. The update_lightning_strikes system's units query will therefore arc-damage ghost units, running damage twice — once per peer.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to ArcTargetFilter at line 39.

findings.description: Doc comment above font_of_life_detect_deaths reads 'Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.' — a copy-paste leftover from the talent-params pattern that appears in casting.rs.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate description, e.g. '/// Tier 3: Font of Life — detects corpses inside the zone and queues them for resurrection.'

findings.description: FIELD_MEDIC_COLOR is typed as a raw (f32, f32, f32, f32) tuple instead of Color, forcing destructuring at every call site. The Font of Life resurrect tint (Color::srgba(0.3, 0.9, 0.3, 1.0) at aura.rs:68) is a nearly-identical unnamed green with no constant at all.
findings.recommendation: Change FIELD_MEDIC_COLOR to type Color. Add a FONT_OF_LIFE_RESURRECT_COLOR: Color constant so both green shades are named and auditable.

findings.description: Inside the per-bolt loop, walls/rocks/trees queries are .collect()-ed into Vec<_> on every active bolt tick. With Thunderstorm talent (3 simultaneous chains) this multiplies the allocations per frame.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the three snapshot Vec collections outside the bolts_to_process loop (before line 94).

findings.description: Uses bare pub use super::casting::* and pub use super::chain::*, exporting everything publicly. Sibling spell modules (mind_control/systems.rs, lightning_rod/systems.rs) use pub(super). Broader visibility is likely unintentional.
findings.recommendation: Tighten to pub(super) use to match the project visibility convention.

findings.description: systems.rs is a pure forwarding proxy re-exporting from both casting::* and vines::*, adding an indirection layer. The plugin reads systems::tick_entangle_ground_effect but the function lives in casting/ground_effect.rs. The file comment admits it is a 're-export hub (Phase 14)', a migration artifact never cleaned up.
findings.recommendation: Remove systems.rs and have plugin.rs import directly from super::casting::* and super::vines::*, mirroring the pattern used by telekinesis and berserker.
