findings.description: nourishing_roots_mana_regen iterates all EntangleRooted entities filtering on talent_params.nourishing_roots every frame whenever any rooted units exist — even when that talent tier/choice is not selected. All EntangleRooted entities from a single cast share identical talent_params, so the filter is all-or-nothing.
findings.recommendation: Gate the system with a has_entangle_talent(1, 2) run condition (matching the pattern in telekinesis/run_conditions.rs) so it only runs when that talent is actually active.

findings.description: vines.rs contains both the pure VFX helper spawn_vine_toruses and the gameplay-affecting apply_entangle which roots units, spawns ground effect entity, and sends pathfinding messages. The file docstring ('vine effects') understates its scope.
findings.recommendation: Rename to entangle_effect.rs or extract apply_entangle into a separate apply.rs alongside root_effects.rs so the file boundary matches its actual responsibility.

findings.description: Three spells (entangle, polymorph, berserker_rage) each define a function named compute_talent_params with the same signature shape (Option<&ActiveTalents>) -> TalentParams. No shared abstraction exists. Telekinesis uses compute_telekinesis_config returning a named struct with pub(super) fields, a clearer approach.
findings.recommendation: No immediate action needed; consider a ComputeTalentParams trait in spells/utils.rs for future spells to standardize the pattern.

findings.description: nearest.as_ref().expect("checked") is technically safe (short-circuit guards it) but violates the project convention that .expect() should be reserved for invariants expressed with a descriptive message, not as a logic proof.
findings.recommendation: Replace with nearest.as_ref().is_some_and(|n| distance < n.3) to make the short-circuit intent explicit without the expect call.

findings.description: Three numeric literals are hardcoded in spawn functions: flash Y position 2.0 (line 84), flash scale 20.0 (line 89), shockwave Y 1.0 (line 111). All other tunable parameters in this module are named constants in constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Extract HARVEST_FLASH_Y, HARVEST_FLASH_SCALE, and SHOCKWAVE_Y into telekinesis/constants.rs for consistency and ease of tuning.

findings.description: berserker_rage_casting_logic receives _clamped_cursor: Option<Vec3> as a parameter but never uses it (leading underscore suppresses the warning). This is dead parameter payload.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused parameter. The caller has clamped_cursor in scope and can pass it back if needed in the future.

findings.description: systems/mod.rs uses pub(crate) mod and pub use re-exports, making most items reachable crate-wide. Only undying_fury_trigger legitimately requires wider visibility (used from game/plugin.rs). Telekinesis uses the tighter pub(super) pattern.
findings.recommendation: Restrict pub use items in berserker_rage/systems/mod.rs to pub(super) except undying_fury_trigger which needs pub for the game/plugin.rs registration.

findings.description: DireSheep has a new() constructor but no Default impl, inconsistent with the project convention for small structs. The new() only initializes attack_timer to a constant — identical to what Default would produce.
findings.recommendation: Implement Default for DireSheep (via attack_timer: DIRE_SHEEP_ATTACK_INTERVAL) and replace DireSheep::new() call sites with DireSheep::default().

findings.description: Team::Defenders.is_enemy(team) is hardcoded as the caster's team perspective in both cast_single_banishment (line 106) and cast_mass_banishment (line 185). In versus-guest mode the local wizard is Team::Attackers, so their enemies are Team::Defenders. The current filter treats Defenders as non-enemies from the Defenders POV, meaning a versus guest finds zero valid targets and can never land a banishment.
findings.recommendation: Inject Option<Res<MultiplayerSession>> into handle_banishment_casting, call local_player_team(session.as_deref()), pass the caster_team into cast_single_banishment and cast_mass_banishment, and replace the two hardcoded Team::Defenders.is_enemy() calls with caster_team.is_enemy(team).

findings.description: spawn_phantom_units iterates all PhantomFogZone entities without excluding GhostSpellEffect ghost zones. Ghost FogCloudZone entities on the guest are spawned with PhantomFogZone { spawn_timer: 0.0 } (ghost_effect_spawn.rs:180). The fog_cloud plugin runs under is_spell_effects_active (guest-inclusive), so after ~3 s the guest ghost zone triggers local phantom unit spawns — real Team::Defenders entities that exist only on the guest, are not networked, and pollute all-unit queries.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostSpellEffect> to the zones query in spawn_phantom_units, matching the host-only intent stated in ghost_effect_spawn.rs comment.

findings.description: apply_fog_cloud_evasion (line 15) and apply_blinding_mist (line 44) both iterate all non-corpse units without excluding GhostEntity. Ghost units have Health and Team. While combat evasion is host-only, the update_timed_modifier::<FogEvasionModifier> system in units/plugin.rs runs on the guest and will tick and remove ghost evasion modifiers every frame, creating spurious ECS churn.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<crate::game::multiplayer::components::GhostEntity> to the targets queries in apply_fog_cloud_evasion and apply_blinding_mist.

findings.description: apply_guardian_circle_buff (line 95) and deal_aoe_force_damage (line 156) use transform.translation.distance(origin) — 3D Euclidean distance. The other three spells in this batch and most of the codebase use xz_distance which ignores Y. This makes Guardian Circle's effective radius slightly smaller for taller units (behemoths, king) and can cause buff misses for units visually inside the circle.
findings.recommendation: Replace .distance() calls on lines 95 and 156 of buff.rs and line 120 of talent_reactions.rs with xz_distance(transform.translation, origin) from crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils.

findings.description: materials.get(&visual_assets.necrotic_pulse).cloned().unwrap_or_default() silently falls back to a default white StandardMaterial if the asset handle is invalid. The explosion spawns with wrong visuals and no log entry to indicate the failure.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a guard: let Some(pulse_material) = materials.get(&visual_assets.necrotic_pulse).cloned() else { warn!("necrotic_pulse material not loaded"); return; };

findings.description: handle_marked_corpses uses 3D distance_squared for the Spreading Blight nearest-enemy search (lines 115-116), while focal_point_retarget in the same file uses manual XZ-only distance on line 193. Inconsistency within the same file; the spreading blight search should also ignore Y for correctness.
findings.recommendation: Replace distance_squared on lines 115-116 with an XZ-only comparison: (a.1.translation.x - t.x).powi(2) + (a.1.translation.z - t.z).powi(2).

findings.description: GuardianCircleShielded is a monolithic struct bundling nine fields for four distinct talent effects (Retaliating Wards, Fortified Resolve, Sanctuary, Martyrdom, Chain Ward). Project convention prefers small focused components queryable with With<T>. All four talent-reaction systems do an if field > 0 check instead of a clean component presence query.
findings.recommendation: Consider splitting into RetaliatingWardsShield, FortifiedResolveShield, SanctuaryShield, MartyrdomShield, ChainWardShield components. Not a blocker.

findings.description: update_sleep_modifiers queries all SleepModifier entities without Without<GhostEntity>. On the guest, ghost units intentionally receive SleepModifier for local visual feedback via status_forwarding. The tick expires and removes SleepModifier (plus NightTerrors, Comatose, NarcolepticWave, Sleepwalking) on ghost units ahead of host-authoritative timing, diverging guest visual state from host truth. Same gap applies to update_night_terrors (line 107) and update_narcoleptic_wave (line 132).
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostEntity> to the query filter in update_sleep_modifiers, update_night_terrors, and update_narcoleptic_wave.

findings.description: update_sleepwalkers overrides TargetingVelocity for all Sleepwalking entities without Without<GhostEntity>. On the guest, ghost units that receive Sleepwalking for visual feedback would have targeting velocity overridden by the guest's LocalSpellOrigin rather than being driven by the host snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostEntity> to the query in update_sleepwalkers.

findings.description: handle_haste_expiry (chain-haste propagation + momentum buff insertion) and tick_haste_slow_zone (applies SlowMovementModifier to units) lack Without<GhostEntity> guards. Chain-haste propagation inserts HasteModifier/ChainHasteSource on additional ghost entities — components not forwarded to the host — causing silent gameplay divergence on the guest side.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostEntity> to all three queries in handle_haste_expiry and to tick_haste_slow_zone's unit query.

findings.description: update_battle_hymn_modifier ticks all BattleHymnModifier entities without Without<GhostEntity>. On the guest, ghost units with BattleHymnModifier (forwarded to host on apply) will have it expired and removed locally ahead of host-authoritative timing. The EchoingSong re-apply path also fires on ghost entities.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostEntity> to the query in update_battle_hymn_modifier.

findings.description: sleep_casting_logic manually re-implements the Pythagorean ground-projected range clamp (lines 193-208) that already exists as clamp_cursor_to_spell_range_with_origin in utils/spell_math.rs. Haste uses the shared helper correctly. The 18-line duplicate will silently drift if the formula changes.
findings.recommendation: Replace lines 191-208 with a call to clamp_cursor_to_spell_range_with_origin(input.cursor_pos, local_origin, wizard.spell_range, effective_radius) and remove the manual wizard_height/max_ground_radius/max_center_distance locals.

findings.description: Magic number 1.4 for Wide Anthem radius multiplier is inlined in a match arm. Analogous values in Haste (ALACRITY_SPEED_MULT) and Sleep (LULLABY_RADIUS_MULT) are named constants in their constants.rs files.
findings.recommendation: Add pub const WIDE_ANTHEM_RADIUS_MULT: f32 = 1.4; to battle_hymn/constants.rs and reference it from the match arm.

findings.description: Chorus of Valor VFX aura is spawned with hardcoded 200.0. constants::CIRCLE_RADIUS is already 200.0 and is used on lines 97, 127, and 198 in the same file. The VFX radius would silently diverge from spell radius if CIRCLE_RADIUS were changed.
findings.recommendation: Replace 200.0 with constants::CIRCLE_RADIUS * primed_spell.empowerment.

findings.description: Five gameplay tuning values are inlined as magic numbers: 1.5 (Inspiring Words duration), 1.5 (War Drums damage), 2.0 (Hymn of Legends double), 0.3 (Anthem Resilience reduction), 20.0 (Fortifying Hymn temp HP), 0.25 (Swift March speed). Haste and Sleep externalise every equivalent value to constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Move to battle_hymn/constants.rs as INSPIRING_WORDS_DURATION_MULT, WAR_DRUMS_DAMAGE_MULT, HYMN_LEGENDS_BONUS_MULT, ANTHEM_RESILIENCE_REDUCTION, FORTIFYING_HYMN_TEMP_HP, SWIFT_MARCH_SPEED_BONUS.

findings.description: Project CLAUDE.md lists commit_spell_cast as an available shared helper in the spells utils section. No function by that name exists anywhere in utils/casting_helpers.rs or the broader codebase. The reference was not removed when the function was renamed or deleted.
findings.recommendation: Remove commit_spell_cast from the CLAUDE.md utils list.

findings.description: audio.rs (432 LOC) mixes three separable concerns: SpellSfxAssets resource + load_spell_sfx_assets startup system (~120 LOC), lookup_sfx_handle/sound_id_kind dispatch (~45 LOC), and all playback helpers (play_sfx, play_looping_sfx, play_sfx_synced, play_remote_sfx, etc. ~265 LOC). Above the 300-line guidance for non-cohesive files.
findings.recommendation: Split into audio/assets.rs (resource + loading), audio/lookup.rs (handle-map + kind dispatch), audio/playback.rs (all play_* helpers). Keep audio.rs or audio/mod.rs as a re-export hub.

findings.description: EYE_SHEET_WIDTH and EYE_SHEET_HEIGHT are private `const` helpers used only to compute EYE_FRAME_UV in the same file. They are not exported yet add named intermediates that leak raw pixel dimensions as named constants when the only meaningful surface is EYE_FRAME_UV.
findings.recommendation: Inline the arithmetic into EYE_FRAME_UV's initializer: `Vec2::new(64.0 / 256.0, 1.0)` with a comment `// 64-px square frame within a 256x64 sheet`. Remove the two intermediate constants.

findings.description: is_on_screen has exactly one call-site (dark_mage/ai/teleport.rs:147). A zero-reuse helper in the shared utils module adds surface area without benefit and may mislead readers into thinking it is widely used.
findings.recommendation: Either inline into dark_mage/ai/teleport.rs (the only consumer) or add a comment documenting the intent to reuse in future bosses so readers understand why it lives here.

findings.description: Visibility inconsistency across sibling module declarations: dark_mage, hags, lich, ray, and components are pub(crate) while ogre and utils are pub(in crate::game). Both choices are correct but the narrower visibility for ogre/utils is silently surprising without explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add brief inline comments on the narrower declarations, e.g. `// no direct UI access; keep game-internal` so the intent is clear.

findings.description: Uses full crate path inline for back_facing_for_velocity and sinusoidal_bob (`crate::game::units::boss::utils::…`) rather than a `use` import at the top of the file. Every other consumer of utils uses a `use` import.
findings.recommendation: Add `use crate::game::units::boss::utils::{back_facing_for_velocity, sinusoidal_bob};` and replace the inline paths with short names. (Owned by lich auditor.)

findings.description: Imports despawn_indicators and indicator_rotation via `use` at line 12 but calls animate_telegraph_material via a full inline path at line 256. Mixed import style in the same file.
findings.recommendation: Add animate_telegraph_material to the existing `use` import at line 12. (Owned by ogre auditor.)

findings.description: martina_mc.rs contains five MindControlled behavior systems (update_mind_controlled_targeting, mind_controlled_pursue_allies, update_mind_control_wear_off, mind_controlled_combat, cleanup_retaliation_targets) with zero Martina-specific code. They are registered by MindControlPlugin (in wizard/spells/mind_control/plugin.rs) and create a hard reverse-dependency from the wizard spell module back into boss/hags/.
findings.recommendation: Move these five functions to wizard/spells/mind_control/systems/mc_behavior.rs (or add to existing effects.rs). Update MindControlPlugin imports. Repurpose martina_mc.rs for Martina's aura (currently in martina_pull.rs).

findings.description: update_mind_controlled_targeting (line 27), update_mind_control_wear_off (line 109), and mind_controlled_combat (line 174) query MindControlled units without Without<GhostEntity>. In multiplayer, status_receive.rs:303 inserts MindControlled onto units by network ID. If ghost units on the host receive MC status, these systems would mutate their TargetingVelocity, tick time_elapsed, and apply damage from ghost MC attackers. mind_controlled_pursue_allies correctly uses Without<GhostEntity> via MindControlPursuitFilter:17.
findings.recommendation: Add Without<GhostEntity> to the controlled query in update_mind_controlled_targeting, update_mind_control_wear_off, and mind_controlled_combat.

findings.description: MindControlled.wear_off_duration is hardcoded to 300.0 (5 minutes) with only an inline comment. No named constant exists anywhere in the hags module for this value, and it differs from all wizard-spell MC durations, making it invisible during balance passes.
findings.recommendation: Add pub const MARTINA_MC_DURATION: f32 = 300.0; to constants.rs and reference it.

findings.description: martina_mind_control (Martina's passive aura) and martina_teleport_pull (cooldown ability) live in the same file named martina_pull.rs. The name implies pull only. The aura is a distinct mechanic with its own data structures and behavior.
findings.recommendation: After H-01 frees up martina_mc.rs, move martina_mind_control into martina_mc.rs so each file has a clear single concern.

findings.description: ChainLightningCooldown::new() initialises time_remaining = 2.0 and FireballCooldown::new() to 5.0, but CHAIN_LIGHTNING_COOLDOWN = 1.0 and FIREBALL_COOLDOWN = 2.0 in constants.rs. The constructors use different values (likely startup-delay offsets) with no documentation explaining why. TeleportPullCooldown::new() similarly sets 6.0 vs constant 2.0.
findings.recommendation: Add named constants CHAIN_LIGHTNING_INITIAL_COOLDOWN, FIREBALL_INITIAL_COOLDOWN, TELEPORT_PULL_INITIAL_COOLDOWN, or add doc comments explaining the offset is an intentional startup-delay stagger.

findings.description: HagEyeState::new() manually constructs {has_invulnerability_eye: false, has_ability_eye: false}. The type should derive Default since both fields are false which is Rust's bool default.
findings.recommendation: Add #[derive(Default)] to HagEyeState; remove or delegate new() to Self::default().

findings.description: Landing pause timer 0.3 is a bare float literal. Every other Josephina timing (LEAP_COOLDOWN, LEAP_FLIGHT_DURATION, MAULING_DURATION) lives in constants.rs; this value was missed.
findings.recommendation: Add pub const LEAP_LANDING_DURATION: f32 = 0.3; to constants.rs and reference it.

findings.description: The invulnerability-eye and ability-eye processing blocks in tick_eye_transfer (lines 103-154 and 157-204) are structurally identical: determine new holder, check if flight needed, despawn old visual, spawn EyeInFlight. A divergence between the two blocks is a maintenance risk.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private fn initiate_eye_transfer(commands, hags, eye_visuals, hag_assets, eye_type, current_holder, new_holder) helper to remove the duplication.

findings.description: use crate::game::constants::* imports the full game constants namespace. Only WIZARD_POSITION and attacker_spawn_position appear to be used from it.
findings.recommendation: Replace with explicit imports: use crate::game::constants::{WIZARD_POSITION, attacker_spawn_position};

findings.description: Beam-steering during-channel logic (dot→angle→max_turn lerp→normalize) is copy-pasted verbatim in petrification.rs:140-152 and beams/mind_control_beam.rs:151-162. The disintegration sweep (movement/disintegration.rs:182-199) carries a 2D rotation variant of the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Extract `steer_beam_toward(current: Vec3, desired: Vec3, turn_rate: f32, delta: f32) -> Vec3` into `beams/beam_helpers.rs` and call it from all three sites.

findings.description: Three identical `has_targets` range-check closures exist in petrification.rs:68-79, movement/disintegration.rs:92-103, and beams/mind_control_beam.rs:75-86. Each iterates defenders, re-runs team_query.get to skip non-Defenders, then checks horizontal distance <= MAX_BEAM_RANGE.
findings.recommendation: Extract `has_defenders_in_range(boss_pos, defenders, team_query, max_range) -> bool` into `beams/beam_helpers.rs` and call it from all three sites.

findings.description: `RayPetrificationBeam` (lines 116-134) and `RayMindControlBeam` (lines 150-168) are structurally identical: both have origin, direction, length, channel_progress, has_fired. Two separate types force near-duplicate visual update systems differing only in beam-width constants.
findings.recommendation: Consider a shared `RayChannelBeam` component. The separate glow/sweep components already differentiate the two for system dispatch.

findings.description: `commands.entity(entity).despawn()` is used for RayBeamVisual lifetime expiry at line 42, while every other despawn in the entire module uses `try_despawn()`. A double-despawn from two racing systems would panic.
findings.recommendation: Change to `commands.entity(entity).try_despawn()` to match the rest of the module.

findings.description: The Fear eye orbit angle is stored in `eye.heading.x` (repurposed as a float angle accumulator). Readers unfamiliar with the special-case branch expect `heading` to be a 2D unit direction, creating a subtle semantic contract violation.
findings.recommendation: Add an `orbit_angle: f32` field to `RayEye` and use it only for Fear eyes, removing the dual-use of `heading.x`.

findings.description: A fresh `StandardMaterial` is allocated via `materials.add(...)` every time the teleport eye fires (once per 15 s cooldown). The bubble material parameters never change between firings.
findings.recommendation: Pre-allocate the bubble material in `preload_ray_assets` (resources.rs), store it in `RayAssets`, and reuse the handle. Alpha fade can be driven by a per-entity component.

findings.description: `update_ray_stalk_particles` accesses `game_rng` (a ResMut) every frame per particle for a random shudder vector, forcing the entire particle update to be single-threaded.
findings.recommendation: Pre-bake a shudder seed into `RayStalkParticle` at spawn time, or derive pseudo-noise from `time.elapsed_secs()` and a per-particle offset to remove the shared-resource dependency.

findings.description: The doc-comment on line 19 ("Attenuated volume for Ray's sound effects...") was copy-pasted from `ray_sfx_volume` in spawn.rs and left attached to the `ray_mind_control_beam` function signature.
findings.recommendation: Remove the stale comment from `ray_mind_control_beam`.

findings.description: `to_body` is computed as `Vec2::new(body_pos.x - my_pos.x, body_pos.z - my_pos.y)` — `.y` on the Vec2 `my_pos` maps to world-Z, not world-Y. Correct by convention but reads misleadingly against the `.z` subscript used elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Rename the intermediate `my_pos` Vec2 to `my_xz` to match `body_xz` used for the Fear eye path (line 63).

findings.description: Stunned and Petrified are referenced inline as fully-qualified crate paths inside query tuple types rather than being added to the existing grouped `use crate::game::units::components::{...}` import block. The same pattern repeats in teleport.rs:44-45. Every other status-effect component in these files is imported at the top.
findings.recommendation: Add `Stunned, Petrified` to the grouped `use crate::game::units::components::{...}` import in both ai_core.rs and teleport.rs.

findings.description: spawn_telegraph_indicators, spawn_meteor_explosion, spawn_lightning_strike, and spawn_plague_cloud are declared `pub(crate)` but are only consumed within the dark_mage module tree. The spells/mod.rs re-exports them as `pub(super)`, so the declaration-level visibility is broader than necessary.
findings.recommendation: Change the four spawn-helper declarations from `pub(crate)` to `pub(super)`. The re-exports in spells/mod.rs already enforce the intended visibility boundary.

findings.description: The module doc comment references an internal refactoring phase number: `//! Re-export hub for dark_mage systems split (Phase 15).` The phase number is meaningless to future readers.
findings.recommendation: Remove `(Phase 15)` from the comment. Rename to `//! Re-exports all dark_mage gameplay systems.`

findings.description: VFX sizing and timing values are scattered inline as magic literals across vfx_updates.rs and spell_spawn.rs: plague particle interval (0.4 s at vfx_updates.rs:73), puff Y range (15.0-45.0 at vfx_updates.rs:80), puff scale range (30.0-55.0 at vfx_updates.rs:86), puff lifetime range (2.0-3.5 at vfx_updates.rs:88), meteor fall time (0.3 s at spell_spawn.rs:180), initial plague puff Y range (20.0-60.0 at spell_spawn.rs:270), initial puff scale range (40.0-70.0 at spell_spawn.rs:276). No matching constants exist in constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Add named constants (PLAGUE_PARTICLE_SPAWN_INTERVAL, PLAGUE_PUFF_Y_MIN/MAX, PLAGUE_PUFF_SCALE_MIN/MAX, PLAGUE_PUFF_LIFETIME_MIN/MAX, METEOR_FALL_DURATION) to constants.rs and replace all inline literals.

findings.description: `let bolt_count = 3` is a local magic number with no corresponding constant. The bolt-spacing formula (LIGHTNING_CORRIDOR_LENGTH / (bolt_count + 1)) is a tuning decision that should be visible alongside other lightning constants.
findings.recommendation: Extract to `pub(super) const LIGHTNING_BOLT_COUNT: usize = 3;` in constants.rs.

findings.description: DarkMageSpellQueue (line 62) and DarkMageEnrage (line 139) both provide `new()` constructors for trivially-constructible zero-state values but do not implement the Default trait. Bevy convention uses Default for no-arg constructors and `new()` for constructors with arguments.
findings.recommendation: Add `impl Default for DarkMageSpellQueue` and `impl Default for DarkMageEnrage` delegating to `new()`, or replace `new()` with `#[derive(Default)]`.

findings.description: ogre_combat's first-pass range check computes attack_range = (boss_hitbox.radius + target_hitbox.radius) * ATTACK_RANGE_MULTIPLIER without adding OGRE_MELEE_RANGE_BONUS. The ogre entity has MeleeRangeBonus(OGRE_MELEE_RANGE_BONUS) inserted at spawn (spawn.rs:104) and the global melee system in combat_systems/melee/combat.rs:229 does add the bonus — but ogre_combat bypasses the global system. The ogre silently has a shorter first-hit trigger range than intended by the component value.
findings.recommendation: Add melee_range_bonus: Option<&MeleeRangeBonus> to the bosses query and add melee_range_bonus.map_or(0.0, |b| b.0) to the attack_range calculation at line 121.

findings.description: use crate::game::units::animation::CombatAnimation bypasses the canonical re-export at crate::game::units::components::CombatAnimation (exposed via pub use super::animation::* in components/mod.rs). All other ogre files import from the components module, making this import inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Change to use crate::game::units::components::CombatAnimation; for consistency with the rest of the module.

findings.description: All three ogre action sites (charge_attack.rs:265, rock_throw.rs:113, melee.rs:136) call crate::game::units::wizard::spells::audio::play_sfx_scaled via fully-qualified inline paths, coupling boss code to the wizard/spells subtree. play_sfx_scaled is a shared utility used by bosses, cauldron, and spells alike.
findings.recommendation: Move play_sfx_scaled to a shared audio module (e.g. src/game/audio.rs). In the meantime, add a use import at the top of each file instead of inline fully-qualified calls.

findings.description: RockThrowCooldown is imported from crate::game::units::brute::components. The ogre borrows a unit-tier component from a sibling unit module with no documentation. A future rename or refactor of brute::components would silently break the ogre.
findings.recommendation: Move RockThrowCooldown to crate::game::units::components (the cross-cutting module) so both brute and ogre import from the canonical location.

findings.description: facing_from_world_direction is a 4-way camera-relative direction helper defined with pub(crate) inside the ogre module. The XZ cam dot-product logic is conceptually identical to back_facing_for_velocity in boss/utils.rs; the two helpers duplicate the camera-relative math pattern.
findings.recommendation: Move facing_from_world_direction to boss/utils.rs alongside back_facing_for_velocity so other boss modules can reuse 4-way facing without re-implementing camera math.

findings.description: ogre_combat iterates the full targets query twice per frame: first pass (lines 109-126) checks for any in-range enemy, second pass (lines 152-186) applies damage. The ogre is a singleton so real cost is negligible, but the double iteration is easy to consolidate.
findings.recommendation: Combine into a single pass that collects hit candidates and applies damage only if a valid target was found.

findings.description: LICH_DAMAGE_MULTIPLIER comment says 'negative = takes less damage from non-spell sources' but DamageMultiplier is applied as the attacker's outgoing modifier (damage * (1 + d.0) in combat_systems/melee/combat.rs:351). A value of -0.5 means the Lich deals 50% less melee damage, not that it takes less damage. The separate LICH_MELEE_DAMAGE_REDUCTION handles incoming resistance.
findings.recommendation: Correct the comment to: '/// Outgoing melee damage penalty — the Lich deals 50% less melee damage.'

findings.description: The Approaching and Combat arms of lich_movement each inline the same steering + damping idiom (target velocity, STEERING_FORCE clamp, VELOCITY_DAMPING.powf damping). The project-wide equivalent lives in units/systems/movement_helpers.rs:224-264. The lich version also skips the speed-scale correction present in the shared helper, meaning at high GLOBAL_SPEED_MULTIPLIER the lich under-accelerates compared to normal units.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small private fn apply_steering(...) helper within movement.rs for both arms, or adapt the lich to call the shared movement helper if it accepts compatible params.

findings.description: Beam target selection uses (kill_stats.elapsed_time * 1000.0) as usize % eligible.len() — a floating-point time cast — instead of GameRng. The index changes every frame until fod.target is set, so the target is deterministic only by accident. All other randomised boss behaviours use GameRng.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a single game_rng.0.gen_range(0..eligible.len()) call (add ResMut<GameRng> param).

findings.description: All public combat system functions are marked pub(crate) but are only ever used within the lich:: subtree (re-exported by systems.rs with pub(super), consumed by plugin.rs). pub(crate) widens visibility crate-wide unnecessarily across all 11 combat functions in animation.rs, beam.rs, soul_power.rs, targeting.rs, and movement.rs.
findings.recommendation: Change all pub(crate) fn in combat/*.rs to pub(super), matching the re-export visibility in systems.rs.

findings.description: The track_soul_power function carries the doc comment verbatim copied from check_lich_spawn: 'Checks if it's time to spawn the Lich mid-game. The Lich spawns as an extra wave after all normal waves have been dispatched…'. This is entirely wrong for the soul power tracking function.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate comment: '/// Accumulates soul power from undead kills during Phase 1 (Summoning).'

findings.description: LichFingerOfDeath::new() is a free constructor but the type has no Default impl. Any future reflection, inspector, or ..Default::default() usage would require a separate addition.
findings.recommendation: Add impl Default for LichFingerOfDeath { fn default() -> Self { Self::new() } }

findings.description: spawn_fresh_undead is a local private helper that manually assembles a unit bundle. It diverges from resurrect_corpse_as_infantry in component set (missing FlockingModifier, OnGameplayScreen) and from the normal infantry spawn helper. A future change to the base undead bundle will silently miss this path.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared spawn_undead_infantry function in units/undead/ that both the lich and the raise_the_dead spell can call, eliminating the divergence.

findings.description: archer_ranged_combat queries &Hitbox (bound as _archer_hitbox) and &mut AttackTiming (bound as _attack_timing) but neither field is read or written. The &mut AttackTiming write-lock prevents Bevy from scheduling this system in parallel with any other system that touches AttackTiming, including archer_melee_combat.
findings.recommendation: Remove both fields from the query tuple. Ranged cooldown is tracked via ArcherMovementTimer, not AttackTiming. The hitbox is irrelevant for ranged range checks.

findings.description: HealerAssets.attacking_texture is loaded at startup via asset_server.load() but is never accessed anywhere in the codebase. The struct-level #[allow(dead_code)] silently suppresses the compiler warning, masking a real GPU texture upload each session.
findings.recommendation: Remove the attacking_texture field, its asset_server.load() call, and its assignment in preload_healer_assets. If a healer attack animation is planned, add it back with a TODO comment.

findings.description: spawn_single_kings_guard derives spawn position from four hardcoded castle corner literals (centroid_x = (-1700 + -1400 + -1700 + -1400) / 4 + 100, centroid_z = ...) rather than using WIZARD_POSITION or defender_spawn_center(). The King spawns via WIZARD_POSITION + radius * angle. If CASTLE_POSITION or WIZARD_OFFSET changes, King and King's Guard silently diverge.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four magic literals with crate::game::constants::defender_spawn_center() (already exists in constants/spawn_math.rs:100) to keep guard spawn in sync with the King's own spawn math.

findings.description: attach_king_spell_shield (line 43) and despawn_king_aura_on_death (line 56) are registered in an add_systems(Update, ...) block with no run_if(is_gameplay_running) guard. Both run every frame regardless of app state (menus, loading, game over), violating the project convention that every Update system must have a run_if guard.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(is_gameplay_running) to the tuple containing these two systems at king/plugin.rs:40-58.

findings.description: Both update_healer_targeting and healer_start_heal_channel independently build an identical Vec<(Entity, Vec3, Team, f32, f32, u32)> ally snapshot from the same potential_targets query every frame, mapping 9 query fields through find_heal_priority. healer_tick_heal_channel uses lazy get_or_insert_with but the other two systems do not.
findings.recommendation: Extract a build_ally_snapshot() helper called once; pass the resulting slice to all three systems. A Local<Vec<_>> populated by the first system in the sequence would avoid both per-frame allocations.

findings.description: spawn_arrow has the doc comment 'Updates archer movement timers to track time since stopped moving.' — copy-pasted from update_archer_movement_timers. The function actually spawns a projectile entity.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment, e.g. 'Spawns a ballistic arrow from origin aimed at target with physics-based trajectory.'

findings.description: update_archer_targeting has the same wrong doc comment 'Updates archer movement timers to track time since stopped moving.' This function sets targeting velocity, not timers.
findings.recommendation: Replace with e.g. 'Sets each archer TargetingVelocity toward the nearest enemy in attack range, applying LOS checks.'

findings.description: check_arrow_collisions has a redundant two-step same-team skip: first 'if *team == arrow.source_team { continue }' then 'let is_enemy = ...; if !is_enemy { continue }'. The first check is a strict subset of the second; any non-enemy including same-team would be caught by is_enemy().
findings.recommendation: Remove the explicit 'if *team == arrow.source_team' guard; is_enemy(team) handles all team combinations.

findings.description: ArcherMovementTimer::new() and HealerAttackTimer::new() both initialise time_since_last_attack to the magic literal 999.0. This value has no relationship to any named cooldown constant and appears in two separate modules.
findings.recommendation: Define a named sentinel constant (e.g. ATTACK_TIMER_READY: f32 = f32::MAX) and use it in both new() implementations for clarity.

findings.description: dispeller/systems/movement.rs and shielder/systems/movement.rs are functionally identical — 137 vs 138 lines — differing only in the marker component (With<Dispeller> vs With<Shielder>). Same CC-immobilize guard, same polymorph-wander block, same calculate_weighted_movement call, same stop-when-still guard. Any future modifier addition must be applied twice.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a generic standard_ground_movement<M: Component>() in units/movement.rs (Bevy 0.18 supports generic systems) and reduce each per-unit file to a one-line call.

findings.description: The polymorphed-wander block (velocity.x.to_bits() as f32 angle, hard-coded speed 20.0) is copy-pasted verbatim across 9+ unit movement files codebase-wide including dispeller (line 97), shielder (line 98), aerialist (line 94), brute, archer, assassin, ogre, hags, infantry. No shared helper exists.
findings.recommendation: Extract apply_polymorph_wander(velocity: &mut Velocity, time: &Time) into units/movement.rs and call it from each unit's movement system.

findings.description: The secondary system groups (tick/refresh/particles) in dispeller and shielder plugins are guarded by any_with_component::<ChannelingCast>. ChannelingCast is also used by healers and wizard channeling spells. These groups therefore pass run-if whenever any healer or wizard channels — even with no dispellers/shielders alive — paying scheduler dispatch cost unnecessarily.
findings.recommendation: Use a compound guard: any_exist::<Dispeller>().and(any_with_component::<ChannelingCast>) in dispeller/plugin.rs (and analogously for shielder).

findings.description: spell_edge_distance is called three times for the winning spell: twice inside the min_by comparator (once per element pair) and once more after min_by to read the final distance. With N dispellable effects and D dispellers this is O(D x N log N x 2) + O(D) redundant calls.
findings.recommendation: Pre-compute (entity, pos, dist) in a single pass before min_by, cache the result, and read dist from the returned element — eliminating the third call entirely.

findings.description: Aerialists receive no CommanderAuraSpeedModifier component at spawn and their custom movement system never queries it. The commander aura system scans all Without<Corpse> units and will silently insert the component onto in-range aerialists, which is never consumed — wasting insert/remove churn and leaving aerialists immune to commander speed buffs with no documentation.
findings.recommendation: Either add CommanderAuraSpeedModifier(0.0) at spawn and apply it in aerialist_movement, or filter aerialists out of the commander-aura affected query with an explicit Without<Aerialist> filter and document the intentional immunity.

findings.description: Aerialist health is expressed inline as crate::game::constants::UNIT_HEALTH * 1.2 with a bare magic multiplier. Every other unit defines a named constant for its health value (e.g. TELEPORTER_HEALTH, DISPELLER_HEALTH).
findings.recommendation: Add pub const AERIALIST_HEALTH: f32 = crate::game::constants::UNIT_HEALTH * 1.2; to aerialist/constants.rs and reference it in spawn.

findings.description: spawn_single_attacker_aerialist accepts _level: u32 (underscore-prefixed, never used). The dead parameter occupies the calling convention without purpose.
findings.recommendation: Remove the parameter and update the call site in loading/queue.rs, or use it to scale health/count if tier scaling is planned.

findings.description: Dispeller and Shielder guard primary systems with the project-local any_exist::<T>() wrapper; Teleporter uses Bevy's built-in any_with_component::<Teleporter>; Aerialist uses any_exist. Two equivalent mechanisms for the same check across the four modules.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on one — prefer Bevy's any_with_component (avoids the custom wrapper) across all four units and the rest of the unit modules.

findings.description: assassin_movement query filter is `With<Assassin>` only — no `Without<Corpse>`. Corpse entities retain Velocity, Acceleration, and MovementSpeed after death; the system will iterate and run full CC checks plus calculate_weighted_movement on them every frame. update_assassin_targeting (line 29) already excludes corpses. Same issue in brute/systems/movement.rs:57 (brute_movement).
findings.recommendation: Add Without<Corpse> to both movement query filters, consistent with all other unit movement systems in the codebase.

findings.description: apply_commander_auras allocates a Vec (commander snapshot via .collect()) and a HashMap<Entity,(Option<f32>,Option<f32>)> from scratch on every frame the run_if condition passes. The King is always present so this runs every gameplay frame with potentially hundreds of units filling the HashMap.
findings.recommendation: Use Local<Vec<_>> and Local<HashMap<_,_>> parameters on the system, clearing them at the top of each call rather than reallocating. Alternatively store state in a CommanderAuraState resource.

findings.description: ASSASSIN_ATTACK_SPEED_BONUS comment says 'Assassin attack speed bonus (2.0 = 3x attack speed)' but the value is 0.0. The comment describes a value that was never set.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite to 'Assassin attack speed bonus. Currently 0.0 (no bonus).' to match reality.

findings.description: ELITE_ATTACK_SPEED_BONUS comment reads '(FUTURE - not implemented in MVP)'. This is wrong: the bonus is queried in combat_systems/melee/combat.rs:252, inserted by loading/upgrade_systems.rs:85, and attached in infantry/systems/spawn.rs:209. The same stale text appears in elite/components.rs:38.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'FUTURE - not implemented in MVP' note from constants.rs and components.rs.

findings.description: AssassinAssets carries attacker_corpse_materials and undead_corpse_materials fields suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)]; they are never read outside resources.rs — cleanup always uses infantry materials. BruteAssets (brute/resources.rs:5) is an empty stub resource inserted at startup but never consumed by any system.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two dead corpse-material fields from AssassinAssets and their construction. Remove BruteAssets entirely along with the preload_brute_assets startup system and its registration in BrutePlugin.

findings.description: Assassin plugin uses any_exist::<Assassin>() (custom wrapper from run_conditions) while brute and commander plugins use any_with_component::<T> (Bevy built-in). Both are functionally identical; the inconsistency creates confusion about which form to prefer.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on any_with_component across all unit plugins. It requires no custom wrapper import.

findings.description: Commander aura distance check uses full 3D Vec3::distance() while assassin targeting (and all other unit targeting) uses XZ-only squared distance. Units are on a flat plane; the 3D form is both inconsistent and slightly slower.
findings.recommendation: Replace unit_transform.translation.distance(*commander_pos) with the XZ-planar distance form matching the rest of the codebase.

findings.description: TeamFilter::Both is marked #[allow(dead_code)] and has zero call sites anywhere in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Remove the variant or add a concrete comment linking it to a specific planned feature to justify keeping the suppressor.

findings.description: spawn_brute doc comment says 'Brutes spawn in the archer row alongside archers' but the inline comment immediately below reads 'Brute spawns at the front with infantry' and the code calls attacker_spawn_position(0, 0.0) — no archer depth offset.
findings.recommendation: Correct the doc comment to match the code and the inline comment.

findings.description: File is 973 LOC containing four unrelated concerns: (1) UI material types — ParchmentMaterial, FrostedGlassMaterial, their marker components and the apply_* systems; (2) page/panel layout factories — spawn_page_container, spawn_left_detail_panel, spawn_right_scroll_panel, spawn_page_header, spawn_button; (3) shared system bodies — escape_to_landing/pause_main/running, handle_main/pause_menu_back_button, handle_scroll, consume_mouse_on_exit, cleanup_screen; (4) a full slider widget — SliderRowConfig, spawn_slider_row, spawn_dot_leader. Violates the project rule that files exceeding ~300 LOC must be split unless every line is a single cohesive match-on-enum or asset registry.
findings.recommendation: Split into: materials.rs (ParchmentMaterial, FrostedGlassMaterial, ParchmentPanel, FrostedGlassOverlay, apply_parchment_backgrounds, apply_frosted_glass_overlays), escape_handlers.rs (escape_to_*, handle_*_back_button, consume_mouse_on_exit, handle_scroll, cleanup_screen), slider.rs (SliderRowConfig, spawn_slider_row, spawn_dot_leader), and a trimmed layout_helpers.rs retaining the panel/button/text spawn helpers (~250 LOC). Update systems.rs re-exports accordingly.

findings.description: Lines 39–42 contain a stale doc comment: '/// Scales a font size down based on text width to fit within a constrained area. /// Returns `base_font` when `max_width <= min_chars`, scaling linearly down to /// `base_font * min_scale` when `max_width >= max_chars`.' This is placed immediately above apply_parchment_backgrounds, which inserts a material on newly-spawned panel entities and has nothing to do with font scaling. The described function does not exist anywhere in the file.
findings.recommendation: Delete lines 39–42 and replace with a correct one-line doc for apply_parchment_backgrounds: '/// Inserts a procedural parchment background material on all newly-added ParchmentPanel entities.'

findings.description: The doc comment for spawn_page_container says 'When `pause_menu` is true, `GlobalZIndex(500)` is added so the page renders above in-game UI.' The actual code at line 250 inserts GlobalZIndex unconditionally — using 1000 for pause_menu=true and 500 for pause_menu=false. The comment omits the non-pause branch entirely and gets the pause-branch value wrong (it is 1000, not 500).
findings.recommendation: Update the doc to: 'A `GlobalZIndex` is always inserted: 1000 for pause overlays (above in-game HUD and spell-book), 500 for normal full-screen pages.'

findings.description: systems.rs is a four-line wildcard re-export hub ('pub use super::button_systems::*; pub use super::layout_helpers::*;'). The project convention reserves systems.rs for system logic bodies and mod.rs for re-exports. This naming inversion means 30+ sub-plugins import shared helpers via 'crate::ui::systems::escape_to_landing' when those helpers actually live in layout_helpers.rs, creating a misleading import path and rustdoc duplication. The file comment says 'Re-export hub for ui systems split (Phase 16)' suggesting it was meant to be transitional.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) move the re-exports to mod.rs where the convention places them, updating all callers (large but mechanical), or (b) rename systems.rs to api.rs or surface.rs with a clear doc that it is a stable re-export surface, not system logic. Option (a) is the correct convention fix; option (b) at least removes the naming lie.

findings.description: spawn_slider_row hard-codes the value display as format!('{}%', (current_value * 100.0) as u32), silently assuming current_value is in [0.0, 1.0]. Callers pass values outside that range: GameSpeed (0.5–2.0), UiBrightness (0.1–2.0), GamepadSensitivityX (0.3–2.5), RogueliteModifier (0.2–3.0). These render as '50%'–'300%'. The update paths (settings interaction and roguelite slider) replicate the same format, so the behavior is consistent — but there is no documented contract in SliderRowConfig and no way for a caller to opt into a different format string.
findings.recommendation: Add a doc comment to SliderRowConfig.current_value explaining the percent convention, and add an optional value_label_fn: Option<fn(f32) -> String> field so callers with non-percentage ranges can supply their own formatter without changing the helper.

findings.description: FrostedGlassMaterial::new() takes no arguments and returns a fixed value. Rust convention (and clippy's new_without_default lint) requires that any pub(crate) struct with a no-argument new() also implements Default. Without it, callers cannot use struct-update syntax or the Default trait bound, and clippy fires in debug builds.
findings.recommendation: Add 'impl Default for FrostedGlassMaterial { fn default() -> Self { Self::new() } }' and optionally derive Default if PaddingData fields can all be derived (they are zero).

findings.description: Twelve Update systems are registered with no run_if guard (update_ui_scale, button_click_detection, button_interaction, reset_deactivated_buttons, sync_front_face_colors, apply_gamepad_focus_tint, apply_flat_gamepad_focus_tint, animate_button_3d, apply_parchment_backgrounds, apply_frosted_glass_overlays, apply_3d_button_structure, enforce_active_button_state). The project convention states 'You MUST only run systems when they need to be run leveraging run_if conditionals.' Most of these have change-detection or Added<> guards so the loop body is a no-op when idle, but they incur scheduler overhead every frame including AppState::Splash and AppState::Loading when no UI entities exist.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the add_systems(Update, ...) call in a .run_if(not(in_state(AppState::Splash))) condition. update_ui_scale could additionally use .run_if(on_event::<WindowResized>()) since scale only needs updating on resize.

findings.description: Bug: spell drag-slider ignores bonus allocations in 'others' sum. handle_detail_slider_interaction computes 'others' by summing only allocation.allocations (spell targets), missing insight already queued to bonus stats. The +/- button path (handle_alloc_adjust_buttons) correctly calls allocation.total_allocated(). When a player drags the spell slider while bonus insight is pending, the slider can over-allocate beyond available insight.
findings.recommendation: Replace the inline .allocations.iter().filter().sum() with allocation.total_allocated() - allocation.get(&spell) to match the +/- button logic.

findings.description: Multiple independent load_unified_save() disk reads per system call. is_spell_unlocked, is_prereq_met, and count_researched_spells each call load_unified_save() separately. During spawn_study_panels they are called per-node for every edge and spell node, producing O(N) file reads. update_graph_node_borders also calls both helpers per node on every selection change.
findings.recommendation: Accept the UnifiedSave once at the callsite and pass the unlocked list down to the helpers, or add a one-frame cache wrapper for load_unified_save().

findings.description: Spell-slider and insight-bonus-slider functionality is nearly identically duplicated across four function pairs: handle_detail_slider_interaction / handle_insight_bonus_slider_interaction, update_detail_sliders / update_insight_bonus_sliders, spawn_detail_unified_slider / spawn_insight_bonus_slider (slider_spawn.rs), and update_allocation_text / update_insight_bonus_allocation_text. Only the component types and a few field names differ.
findings.recommendation: Extract shared drag-tracking and visual-sync logic into generic helpers parameterized on the component type, and a shared spawn_unified_slider_body function.

findings.description: update_graph_node_label_scale (a graph-view system driven by GraphViewState) and update_star_sky_time (a material animation system) are placed in slider_systems.rs despite having no relationship to sliders. This misplacement makes the file's responsibility unclear.
findings.recommendation: Move update_graph_node_label_scale to positions.rs. Move update_star_sky_time to graph_nav.rs or a new graph_animation.rs.

findings.description: helpers.rs mixes two unrelated concerns: save-data accessors (is_spell_unlocked, is_prereq_met, count_researched_spells) and pure geometry math (graph_to_screen, clip_line_to_rect, compute_slider_fracs). Feature-slicing rules call for concern-focused files.
findings.recommendation: Split into helpers.rs (save-data helpers only) and geometry.rs (pure math functions).

findings.description: update_graph_node_borders calls is_spell_unlocked and is_prereq_met per graph node, each loading the save from disk. The system is gated on resource_changed::<SelectedStudySpell> so it doesn't run every frame, but when it fires it issues 2xN disk reads for all spell nodes.
findings.recommendation: Pre-load the save once at the top of update_graph_node_borders and pass the unlocked list directly to the helpers.

findings.description: The placeholder Text node 'Select a spell or bonus to view details' is spawned identically in both update_insight_detail_panel (insight_detail.rs:36) and update_study_detail_panel (spell_detail.rs:44). Any change to the wording must be made in two places.
findings.recommendation: Extract a spawn_placeholder_text(panel) helper in detail_panel/mod.rs and call it from both sites.

findings.description: random_seed() is defined identically in both init.rs:9 and seed_input.rs:11. Both call rand::rng().random_range(0..constants::MAX_SEED). Two copies will silently diverge if the range or RNG is ever changed.
findings.recommendation: Extract a single pub(super) fn random_seed() -> u64 in constants.rs and call it from both init.rs and seed_input.rs.

findings.description: ModifierSliderValue methods (get, set, min_value, max_value, step, label) are declared pub instead of pub(crate). The containing enum is pub(crate), so the extra visibility leaks a wider contract surface than needed.
findings.recommendation: Change all six method signatures from pub to pub(crate).

findings.description: toggle_expand_action declares two separate queries for ToggleExpandButton: expand_buttons: Query<&ToggleExpandButton> (used only for the early-return lookup) and expand_btn_entities: Query<(Entity, &ToggleExpandButton)> (used to mutate ButtonActive). One query covering (Entity, &ToggleExpandButton) would serve both purposes.
findings.recommendation: Merge into a single Query<(Entity, &ToggleExpandButton)> and obtain the component via .get(event.button) directly.

findings.description: The border-color update loop (for mut border in &mut border_query at line 138-145) is located outside the for event in button_clicked.read() loop, so it writes to BorderColor every frame regardless of whether any click occurred. Writes to BorderColor mark entities changed and trigger unnecessary Bevy change-detection work.
findings.recommendation: Gate the loop behind a focus_changed boolean set inside the event loop, or move the border update to run only when seed_state.is_changed().

findings.description: Seed input border colors are hardcoded as Color::hsla(270.0, 0.35, 0.35, 1.0) (unfocused, appears 5 times across lines 52, 79, 83, 143, 245) and Color::hsla(270.0, 0.65, 0.55, 1.0) (focused, lines 141 and in keyboard handler). These are absent from constants.rs so they cannot be changed in one place.
findings.recommendation: Add SEED_INPUT_BORDER_UNFOCUSED and SEED_INPUT_BORDER_FOCUSED constants to constants.rs and replace all occurrences.

findings.description: Comment reads '// Enter/Escape to unfocus' but the condition on line 234 only checks KeyCode::Enter and KeyCode::NumpadEnter. KeyCode::Escape is absent — the feature was either never implemented or silently removed.
findings.recommendation: Either add || keyboard.just_pressed(KeyCode::Escape) to the condition to match the comment, or update the comment to say 'Enter to unfocus'.

findings.description: The 'apply a fresh random seed when text is empty' pattern is duplicated three times: seed_input_click lines 118-122, seed_input_click lines 128-133, and seed_input_keyboard lines 237-242. Each copy sets seed_state.text, config.seed, and updates all SeedInputText nodes.
findings.recommendation: Extract a fn apply_random_seed(seed_state, config, text_query) helper and call it from the three sites.

findings.description: format!("{:?}", wizard_type) used as a stable identifier for save-file name matching in four in-scope sites (wizard_cards.rs:167, wizard_cards.rs:453, multiplayer_tab/state.rs:186, layout/setup/resources.rs:14). Debug output is not a stable serialisation contract — a variant rename or custom Debug impl silently breaks all existing player save comparisons with no compile error.
findings.recommendation: Add fn save_key(&self) -> &'static str to WizardType and Spell returning a canonical name string. Replace all format!("{:?}", wt) comparisons with wt.save_key().

findings.description: spawn_coop_gated_button is a UI helper function living in constants/dimensions.rs. Project rules forbid mixing behaviour into constant files. The function is shared by endless_tab.rs and two roguelite_tab/ files.
findings.recommendation: Move spawn_coop_gated_button and its GUEST_NOT_READY_BUTTON_STYLE companion to a coop_button.rs sibling file, or into ui/systems.rs if truly cross-cutting.

findings.description: text_input.rs hardcodes Color::hsla(270.0, 0.65, 0.55, 1.0) and Color::hsla(270.0, 0.35, 0.35, 1.0) as inline literals. The identical colors are already named CODE_BOX_BORDER_FOCUSED and CODE_BOX_BORDER_UNFOCUSED in panel_styles.rs:20-21. Two sources of truth for the same visual value.
findings.recommendation: Import and use CODE_BOX_BORDER_FOCUSED / CODE_BOX_BORDER_UNFOCUSED from panel_styles.rs in text_input.rs.

findings.description: MultiplayerPanelData is a #[derive(SystemParam)] used by exactly one system (rebuild_panels_on_tab_change). Project conventions say to only use SystemParam when a group is reused across 3+ systems with identical parameter sets. Here it wraps 4 resources and exists only for a single caller.
findings.recommendation: Inline the four resources directly into rebuild_panels_on_tab_change. The function has ~13 current parameters, fitting within Bevy's 16-parameter limit.

findings.description: broadcast_host_mode_to_guest runs every Update frame. On the roguelite-no-run path the early-return is skipped unconditionally, so roguelite_summary_lines() is called and a Vec<String> is allocated each frame even when nothing changed, then compared and discarded.
findings.recommendation: Gate the roguelite-no-run rebuild on resource_changed::<RogueliteModifiers>.or(resource_changed::<PendingToggles>), or cache detail_lines in a Local and rebuild only on actual change.

findings.description: File is named panel_styles.rs — a near-variant of the forbidden styles.rs name. Content is constants-only and fine, but the name signals the forbidden pattern and will confuse future reviewers.
findings.recommendation: Rename to panel_constants.rs for unambiguity and consistency with project naming conventions.

findings.description: A `use crate::ui::constants::efficiency_color;` import appears mid-file between two function bodies rather than at the top-level imports block. Reads as a stale comment or accidental placement.
findings.recommendation: Move the use import to the top of the file with other imports.

findings.description: spawn_controls_tab calls crate::config::save_data::load_unified_save() — a synchronous filesystem read — inside a builder fn invoked from rebuild_settings_content, an Update system. I/O latency or failure is silently swallowed via .unwrap_or_default(), causing all archetypes to appear locked on transient read failure. The save is already loaded and cached at startup; no reason to re-read it here.
findings.recommendation: Pass the unlocked wizard list as a parameter derived from an already-loaded Bevy resource (Res<SaveData> or a thin Res<UnlockedWizards>). Eliminate the direct disk read from the spawn path.

findings.description: Three 'action button' rows (Reset Tutorials at game_tab.rs:84-131, Clear Progress at game_tab.rs:133-181, Reset Controls at controls_tab.rs:208-255) each inline ~47 lines of identical Node spawn boilerplate instead of using the existing spawn_option_row + spawn_option_button helpers from setup.rs. The helpers already accept a generic Bundle action component.
findings.recommendation: Add a spawn_action_button(parent, label, action: impl Bundle, is_danger: bool) helper in setup.rs and replace all three inline blocks. Removes ~90 lines of duplication.

findings.description: handle_confirmation_popup carries a copy-paste doc comment from builders/setup.rs that says it 'Sets up the settings menu UI with a tabbed interface'. The actual function handles confirmation popup clicks and Back-gamepad dismissal.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc comment: '/// Handles confirmation popup button clicks and Back-gamepad dismissal.'

findings.description: The doc comment '/// Opens key capture overlay when a binding button is clicked.' appears on two consecutive lines (20 and 21) — a paste artifact.
findings.recommendation: Delete the duplicate line 21.

findings.description: Stale comment: '// NOTE: The rest of this function was the old placeholder. The spawn_controls_subsection and spawn_key_binding_row helpers are defined below.' Refers to a removed previous implementation and adds no information.
findings.recommendation: Remove the stale comment. The helper names are self-documenting.

findings.description: Module doc '//! Re-export hub for settings systems split (Phase 16).' references an internal development phase number that is meaningless to future readers.
findings.recommendation: Replace with '//! Re-exports all settings systems for external use.'

findings.description: Doc comment on `update_mana_bar` reads 'Blocks spell input when the mouse is interacting with a UI button…' — the doc for `block_spell_input_on_button_interaction`, copy-pasted during the Phase-16 file split.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc describing mana + reserved-mana bar width updates based on wizard mana and concentration-spell costs.

findings.description: Identical stale 'Blocks spell input…' comment appears above `update_wave_display`. Same copy-paste artifact from the Phase-16 split.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct one-liner: 'Updates the wave counter text when WaveState changes.'

findings.description: Bottom-bars section (ammo-display branch, mana+reserved-fill branch, cast-bar+brewing-overlay block) is duplicated verbatim across hud_sp.rs (~85-90 lines, lines 208-349) and hud_mp.rs (lines 101-239). `spawn_king_health_bar` was extracted for exactly this reason; the bottom bars were not.
findings.recommendation: Extract `fn spawn_bottom_bars(bars: &mut ChildSpawnerCommands, config: &GameConfig)` into a shared helper and call it from both builders.

findings.description: `spawn_hag_bar_section` (lines 215-281) and `spawn_ray_eye_bar_section` (lines 283-345) are structurally identical: same child layout, background, border, text overlay. They differ only in the component marker types attached to fill/text nodes.
findings.recommendation: Extract a generic `fn spawn_boss_bar_section<F: Component, T: Component>(parent, fill_marker, text_marker, name, color, ...)` helper and call it from both sites.

findings.description: `HagIdentity` to usize index mapping (Justina=0, Martina=1, Josephina=2) is repeated three times in `update_boss_health_bar` (lines 103, 114, 127). `RayEyeType` has an `index()` method for the same purpose; `HagIdentity` does not.
findings.recommendation: Add `pub const fn index(self) -> usize` to `HagIdentity` in `game/units/boss/hags/components.rs` and replace all three match blocks with `.index()`.

findings.description: Boss-type detection uses `.iter().next().is_some()` six times (lines 28-33). The idiomatic Bevy form is `!query.is_empty()`, which is used everywhere else in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Replace all six `.iter().next().is_some()` calls with `!query.is_empty()`.

findings.description: `spawn_boss_health_bar` runs every frame during gameplay, evaluating six queries even after the bar has been spawned once. After the first spawn `boss_exists && !bar_exists` is always false, but queries still execute at 60 fps for the entire boss fight.
findings.recommendation: Add `.run_if(not(any_with_component::<BossHealthBarRoot>))` alongside `is_gameplay_running` in plugin.rs to skip the system entirely once the bar exists.

findings.description: Ray eye bar section colors are inline Color::srgb literals. The hag identity colors are defined in constants.rs; Ray eye colors are not, creating inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Add `RAY_EYE_PETRIFICATION_COLOR`, `RAY_EYE_DISINTEGRATION_COLOR`, etc. to `constants.rs` and reference them from the spawn array.

findings.description: Tooltip top-offset is `BUFF_BOX_SIZE + BUFF_BOX_GAP + 20.0 + 10.0`; the two bare addends are unexplained magic numbers (likely HUD margin + extra padding).
findings.recommendation: Replace bare floats with named constants or add an inline comment explaining what each addend represents.

findings.description: PauseMenuCompendiumPlugin does not register systems::update_item_active_state or systems::handle_copy_seed. In the pause-menu compendium: selected item buttons are never highlighted, and the 'Copy Seed' button on a roguelite run silently does nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add both systems to PauseMenuCompendiumPlugin's Update blocks, mirroring the MainMenuCompendiumPlugin registration at lines 34 and 46.

findings.description: rebuild_on_state_change is 253 lines with four distinct responsibilities: tab-button visual update, save-data load + item-list rebuild, update_detail_panel dispatch, and level-history container show/hide. The function also carries a Bevy 16-param tuple workaround comment.
findings.recommendation: Extract update_tab_visuals and update_level_history_container as free helper functions, reducing the system body to an orchestrator.

findings.description: update_detail_panel is 415 lines and accepts 14 parameters. Each of the seven CompendiumItemId match arms independently updates the same five query references plus icon, with no arm-level extraction.
findings.recommendation: Extract each match arm to show_spell_detail, show_unit_detail, etc. free functions; update_detail_panel becomes a thin dispatcher.

findings.description: Team grouping uses raw string literals &["Defender", "Attacker", "Boss"] that must exactly match UnitType::team_label() return values. A rename silently breaks grouping with no compile error.
findings.recommendation: Extract to a const array or add a UnitType::teams() iterator yielding (label, color) pairs to couple the label strings to their source of truth.

findings.description: Victory green Color::srgb(0.3,0.8,0.3), defeat red Color::srgb(0.8,0.3,0.3), and accent blue Color::srgb(0.3,0.6,0.9) appear as inline literals across at least four sites with no named constants.
findings.recommendation: Add VICTORY_COLOR, DEFEAT_COLOR, ACCENT_COLOR to constants.rs and reference them from all call sites.

findings.description: systems.rs is a pure re-export shim that exists only so plugin.rs can write systems::handle_tab_click. The 'Phase 16' comment suggests a migration artifact. It adds an opaque three-hop indirection layer (plugin -> systems -> setup/mod -> handlers).
findings.recommendation: Remove systems.rs and import directly from super::setup in plugin.rs, or document the shim role and drop the historical comment.

findings.description: items_container.single() failure on the tab-changed branch is silently skipped. If more than one ItemsContainer entity exists, the item list is never rebuilt with no log warning.
findings.recommendation: Add warn!("Expected exactly one ItemsContainer") in the failed branch since this is a programming invariant violation, not a normal runtime condition.

findings.description: `enforce_tutorial_modality` and `drain_pending_tutorials` run unconditionally in Update every frame with no state or resource guard. Both have cheap `Option<Res<ActiveTutorial>>` early returns but Bevy still schedules and enters both systems on every frame across all game states, including in-game combat, even when no tutorial is active or pending.
findings.recommendation: Add `.run_if(resource_exists::<ActiveTutorial>)` to `enforce_tutorial_modality` and a combined condition to the chained block. `drain_pending_tutorials` can also gate on `resource_exists::<PendingTutorials>`.

findings.description: `try_start_tutorial` accepts a `pending: Option<&PendingTutorials>` parameter then immediately discards it with `let _ = pending;`. The function instead accesses `PendingTutorials` through a deferred `commands.queue` world closure. The parameter misleads callers into thinking their borrow is consumed.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `pending` parameter from `try_start_tutorial` and update all six call sites to omit it. The world-command path already safely acquires `PendingTutorials` without the caller's borrow.

findings.description: `_wt_buttons: Query<(Entity, &WizardTowerButtonAction), Without<TutorialHighlightable>>` is declared with an underscore prefix to silence the warning, but its body is never iterated. Bevy still resolves and allocates this query every frame that `ActiveTutorial` exists. `WizardTowerButtonAction` is imported solely for this dead parameter.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead `_wt_buttons` parameter and the unused `WizardTowerButtonAction` import on line 10. If `StartBattleButton` / `TimeTravelButton` highlighting is needed again, add it explicitly then.

findings.description: `update_tutorial_content` walks `Children` two levels deep (children then grandchildren) to update the 'Next'/'Got it' button text label. This relies on `spawn_button`'s internal node structure remaining stable. Any layout refactor that adds or removes a wrapper node silently breaks the label update with no compile-time error.
findings.recommendation: Tag the button's text child with a `TutorialNextButtonLabel` marker component at spawn time in `overlay.rs`. Then `update_tutorial_content` can query `(&mut Text, With<TutorialNextButtonLabel>)` directly, removing all tree traversal.

findings.description: `TutorialProgress::completed` is `Vec<String>`. Both `is_completed` and `mark_completed` allocate a `String` via `.to_string()` and perform an O(n) linear scan on every call. With ~12 IDs today this is trivially cheap, but `Vec<String>` gives no uniqueness guarantee at the type level.
findings.recommendation: Change `completed` to `HashSet<String>` for O(1) lookup and structural uniqueness. `mark_completed` can drop its manual duplicate check. Ensure `#[serde(default)]` is already present (it is).

findings.description: Three static step arrays (`WIZARD_TOWER_STEPS`, `TIME_TRAVEL_STEPS`, `STUDY_STEPS`) belong to deprecated `TutorialId` variants (`WizardTowerIntro`, `TimeTravelIntro`, `StudyIntro`). No live trigger ever fires those IDs. The arrays add ~90 lines of unreachable content. Their `HighlightTarget` variants (`StartBattleButton`, `TimeTravelButton`) are also never tagged by any tagging system.
findings.recommendation: Replace the step arrays for deprecated IDs with `&[]` empty slices to make the dead content obvious and trimmed while keeping the ID variants for save-compat.

findings.description: The doc comment on `tag_wizard_tower_entities` reads: 'Starts a tutorial if it hasn't been completed and tutorials are enabled. If another tutorial is already active, appends this one to PendingTutorials…'. This is a verbatim copy-paste of `try_start_tutorial`'s documentation and has nothing to do with entity tagging.
findings.recommendation: Replace the comment with: 'Tags Wizard Tower UI entities with `TutorialHighlightable` so the highlight system can find them.'

findings.description: `PanelAnchor::TopCenter` is marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` — it is defined but never referenced in any step array or live code path. It is dead content with a suppressor.
findings.recommendation: Either remove `TopCenter` entirely, or remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` so the compiler flags it at the next step-content edit.

findings.description: Brew-preview rendering (~100 lines) is copy-pasted between update_detail_panel_on_selection_change (ingredient_clicks.rs:81-203) and spawn_detail_panel (setup/detail_panel.rs:77-207). Includes ingredient count string, brew-time Alchemist multiplier, duration multiplier, effects list, dilution block, and combo block. A future change to any of these must be applied in both places and can silently diverge.
findings.recommendation: Extract a spawn_brew_preview_children(parent, selection, recipe, is_alchemist, unlocked_combos) helper into setup/detail_panel.rs and call it from both the full-spawn and incremental-rebuild paths.

findings.description: The doc comment on button_action reads 'Spawns the cauldron menu UI when entering the CauldronMenu state.' — which is the doc comment for spawn_cauldron_menu_ui copied onto the wrong function. button_action handles click/action dispatch and state transitions, not spawning.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment describing click handling and state transition dispatch.

findings.description: DETAIL_LABEL_COLOR (line 52), INGREDIENT_COUNT_FULL_COLOR (line 70), and COMBO_COLOR (line 88) are three separately-named constants all with the identical value Color::hsla(270.0, 0.50, 0.60, 1.0). This creates confusion about whether they are intentionally distinct values.
findings.recommendation: Unify as a single named constant (e.g., ACCENT_PURPLE) and either alias or replace the three names, or add an explicit comment confirming they are intentionally the same accent color.

findings.description: BREW_BUTTON_STYLE and CANCEL_BUTTON_STYLE hardcode width: 160.0, height: 40.0, border_width: 1.0 as raw literals, while all five ingredient/stone button styles (lines 147-208) correctly reference the named constants BUTTON_WIDTH, BUTTON_HEIGHT, BUTTON_BORDER_WIDTH. If button size changes, action buttons will silently diverge.
findings.recommendation: Replace the raw literals in BREW_BUTTON_STYLE and CANCEL_BUTTON_STYLE with BUTTON_WIDTH, BUTTON_HEIGHT, and BUTTON_BORDER_WIDTH.

findings.description: update_detail_panel_on_selection_change has a redundant internal early-exit guard (if !selection.is_changed() { return; }) even though it is already registered with .run_if(resource_changed::<IngredientSelection>) in plugin.rs:47. The inner guard is dead code in normal operation and misleading.
findings.recommendation: Remove the if !selection.is_changed() guard from inside the system body — the outer run_if is sufficient.

findings.description: build_menu references crate::ui::main_menu::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE (150x50, border 2px) rather than crate::ui::constants::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE (140x50, border 3px). Other in-game overlays (spell_book, manual) use the shared constant. The cauldron back button is visually larger than other in-game back buttons.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether the size difference is intentional. If not, switch to crate::ui::constants::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE to be consistent with other in-game overlays.

findings.description: ActionBarSlotText is defined and used as a query filter in three systems (keyboard_highlight.rs:36,45 and radial.rs:69,79,92) but is never spawned anywhere. Spell names were removed from action bar slots (see spawn.rs:219-226 comment and the suppressed `let _ = slot_name`). The dead component, the slot_text_query in update_action_bar_slots, and the name_texts query in animate_action_bar_layout are all unreachable code that mislead readers and add noise to Bevy query archetypes.
findings.recommendation: Delete ActionBarSlotText, remove slot_text_query from update_action_bar_slots, remove the name_texts query and text-display block from animate_action_bar_layout. Also remove the dead slot_name binding and suppression in spawn.rs:119-226.

findings.description: handle_slot_click and handle_keyboard_input contain near-identical dispatch logic (Warglock -> select_gun; exclusive-casting -> no-op; else -> prime_spell) but check the exclusive-casting guard differently. handle_slot_click (line 34) calls config.wizard_type.uses_exclusive_casting() while handle_keyboard_input (line 65) does a manual matches!(…, RuneCaster | Randomancer). A new exclusive-casting archetype would update uses_exclusive_casting() but silently miss the manual match.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared dispatch_action_slot(slot_idx, &config, mp_session, &mut prime_spell, &mut select_gun) helper called by both handlers. This eliminates the duplication and ensures consistent use of uses_exclusive_casting().

findings.description: animate_action_bar_layout iterates slots.iter_mut() a second time solely to write justify_content. The value (text_hidden) is computed before the first loop at line 124, so justify_content can be assigned inside that loop. The second pass exists only because the borrow was released to do the children walk in between.
findings.recommendation: Move the justify_content assignment into the existing first loop (line 124), eliminating the redundant second mutable borrow of slots.

findings.description: SPELL_NAME_FONT_SIZE carries the doc comment 'Increased to 16.0 for better readability with multiline names.' but its current value is 7.0. The '16.0' figure refers to a previous value that was reverted. Spell names were subsequently removed from slots entirely, making this comment doubly misleading.
findings.recommendation: Remove the stale 'Increased to 16.0' sentence and replace with a plain description of the constant's purpose.

findings.description: The gunslinger selected-gun slot highlight uses the inline magic color Color::srgb(1.0, 0.8, 0.2) rather than a named constant. RADIAL_HOVER_COLOR exists (Color::srgba(1.0, 0.95, 0.4, 1.0)) but the two gold shades are slightly different. The unnamed color makes the intent opaque.
findings.recommendation: Define a GUN_SELECTED_SLOT_COLOR constant in constants.rs (or reuse RADIAL_HOVER_COLOR if the shades should converge) and reference it from keyboard_highlight.rs.

findings.description: slot_name is computed in spawn_action_bar as the first element of a tuple destructure and immediately suppressed with `let _ = slot_name` at line 226. The comment explains spell names are no longer rendered, but the binding still forces a spell.map(|s| s.name()) call on every slot per spawn.
findings.recommendation: Remove slot_name from the destructure and replace the tuple with `let icon_handle: Option<Handle<Image>> = …`. Remove `let _ = slot_name`.

findings.description: Efficiency calculation (1.0 - defenders_killed / total_defenders) is duplicated three times: saves.rs:38-45, saves.rs:235-241, and screen/layout.rs:57. Each copy has minor surface variation (one multiplies by 100, two differ in variable naming). Any change to this canonical game metric must be made in three places.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn calculate_efficiency(kill_stats: &KillStats) -> f32 returning a [0,1] ratio into saves.rs and call it from all three sites.

findings.description: The hotkey-button visual update loop (iterate all_hotkey_buttons, insert/remove ButtonActive + ButtonColors based on config.action_bar_slots) is copy-pasted identically between handle_hotkey_click (lines 211-231) and handle_number_key_assignment (lines 259-278). Both blocks are 18 lines of identical ECS command patterns.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn sync_hotkey_button_visuals(commands, buttons, config, spell) as a private helper and call it from both handlers.

findings.description: The doc comment on setup_game_over_screen says 'Saves efficiency for current level to config' and 'This system runs BEFORE setup_game_over_screen'. Both claims are false: the function only spawns the score-screen UI. The comment was copy-pasted from the sibling save_efficiency_to_config system in saves.rs.
