findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate one-liner: 'Spawns the score-screen UI entities based on the current game outcome, kill stats, and run state.'

findings.description: button_action and relabel_continue_for_coop are declared pub (bare crate-public) but are only ever consumed by the sibling plugin.rs via use super::systems::*. No external module imports them directly.
findings.recommendation: Change both to pub(super) and update the re-export in systems/mod.rs to pub(super) use actions::*.

findings.description: MpPauseSettingsPlugin (138 LOC) and PauseSettingsPlugin (85 LOC) are structurally identical: same imported systems, same Update batches, same ButtonActionSet grouping, identical debug-assertions block. They differ only in back-state target and escape handler name. All shared Update systems are registered twice, independently.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn register_settings_systems<S: States + FreelyMutableState>(app, state) and call it from both plugins, keeping only the back-action system and escape handler state-specific.

findings.description: nearest_in_direction materialises candidates: impl IntoIterator into a Vec unconditionally at line 76, even though the horizontal-nav single-pass branch only iterates it once. This allocation occurs on every focus-navigation input frame.
findings.recommendation: For the horizontal branch, iterate the IntoIterator directly without collecting. Collect to a slice only for the vertical two-pass branch that must call nearest_pass twice.

findings.description: Seed display (small grey text, 'Seed: {}', font_size 14.0, Color::srgba(0.6,0.6,0.6,0.8), absolute-positioned) is copy-pasted with identical node parameters and styling in both game_over/screen/layout.rs:403-416 and pause_menu/main/systems/spawn.rs:315-327.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn spawn_seed_label(parent: &mut ChildSpawnerCommands, seed: u64) into ui/systems.rs and call it from both sites.

findings.description: rune_display has no OnExit(InGameState::Running) cleanup. When the player pauses (Running→Paused) and resumes (Paused→Running) in SP, OnEnter(InGameState::Running) fires again and spawns a second rune display on top of the first. roulette_display explicitly guards against this; rune_display does not.
findings.recommendation: Add OnExit(InGameState::Running) with cleanup_screen::<RuneDisplayRoot> and OnExit(MultiplayerGameState::Running) with the same, mirroring roulette_display.

findings.description: arcanorouter_display has no OnExit cleanup at all (neither SP nor MP). ArcanoRouterDisplay is tagged OnGameplayScreen which is only cleaned at AppState::InGame exit, not at pause/unpause boundaries. Same duplicate-spawn-on-pause class of bug as rune_display.
findings.recommendation: Add OnExit(InGameState::Running) and OnExit(MultiplayerGameState::Running) with cleanup_screen::<ArcanoRouterDisplay>.

findings.description: roulette_display spawns on OnEnter(MultiplayerGameState::Running) but has no matching OnExit(MultiplayerGameState::Running) cleanup. The SP comment at line 15 explaining the duplicate-prevention was not extended to the MP spawn path.
findings.recommendation: Add OnExit(MultiplayerGameState::Running) with cleanup_screen::<RouletteDisplayRoot>, matching the SP pattern at lines 21-22.

findings.description: queue_notifications runs unconditionally in Update every frame across all app states including splash, menus, and loading screens, where all five message channels will always be empty. The two sibling systems in the same block both have run_if guards; this one does not.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the entire (queue_notifications, ...).chain() set with a run_if(is_gameplay_running.or(in_state(AppState::MainMenu))) condition covering states where toasts can actually appear.

findings.description: update_weather_buttons hard-codes the keyboard hint 'Clear Skies — Press Q/W/E' with no gamepad adaptation, while the two peer archetype overlays (adapt_rune_labels_to_input_device, adapt_prompt_to_input_device) both swap text/font for the active controller style. A Meteorologist using a gamepad sees a keyboard prompt.
findings.recommendation: Add an adapt_weather_prompt_to_input_device system (modeled on roulette_display's adapter) that replaces Q/W/E with D-pad glyphs when a gamepad is active, and register it in weather_bar/plugin.rs.

findings.description: ParsedManualContent is a Resource defined inside systems.rs. Project convention places components and resources in components.rs (or a dedicated file), keeping systems.rs free of type definitions.
findings.recommendation: Move ParsedManualContent to manual/components.rs alongside ManualTab and the other manual-screen types.

findings.description: NotificationQueue::pop calls Vec::remove(0), an O(n) front-removal that shifts all remaining entries. Notification bursts (new wizard + chain of ingredient/spell toasts) make this worst-case linear.
findings.recommendation: Replace Vec<NotificationEntry> with std::collections::VecDeque<NotificationEntry> and change remove(0) to pop_front(). push stays as-is (push_back).

findings.description: adapt_rune_labels_to_input_device runs every gameplay frame with no change guard, iterating all four rune-button entities each tick. The body's equality checks prevent actual writes but the iteration still runs unconditionally.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(resource_changed::<ActiveInputDevice>.or(resource_changed::<CurrentControllerGlyphStyle>)) in the plugin; keep the body's equality checks as safety nets.

findings.description: animate_wheel_spin accesses SPIN_DURATION via a 7-segment absolute crate path (crate::game::units::wizard::archetypes::roulette::constants::SPIN_DURATION) instead of a use import at the top of the file.
findings.recommendation: Add a use crate::game::units::wizard::archetypes::roulette::constants::SPIN_DURATION; import at the top of roulette_display/systems.rs.

findings.description: .expect("UI root exists") is used inside a branch entered only when has_ui == true, making the panic logically unreachable. A future refactor changing the early-return structure could silently introduce a real panic.
findings.recommendation: Replace with if let Some(root) = ui_root_query.iter().next() { root } else { return; } to make the invariant structural rather than asserted at runtime.

findings.description: tracking.rs houses two substantial system functions (reset_all_achievements at line 71 and init_achievements at line 149) inside the resources/ subtree. Convention says resources/ files hold resource types and their constructors only; system bodies belong in systems.rs or dedicated feature files.
findings.recommendation: Move reset_all_achievements and init_achievements to a new src/game/achievements/init.rs. Keep tracking.rs as resource types + MultiKillTracker impl only.

findings.description: Roguelite modifier achievements use an abbreviated Ach suffix (e.g., ModWaveSpeedMinAch, ModAll200Ach) while every other achievement resource uses the full Achievement suffix (e.g., FirstVictoryAchievement, ClickerAchievement). 16 types are inconsistently named, creating friction when searching the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Rename all 16 Mod*Ach types to Mod*Achievement. Also update tracking.rs and modifier_checks.rs.

findings.description: check_master_brewer uses format!("{:?}", i) to build string keys for checking the save's ingredient set. The Debug repr must exactly match the string used when writing the unlock. If any Ingredient variant is renamed, existing player saves will silently fail to match and the achievement will never fire.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared ingredient_key(i: Ingredient) -> String function used both when writing (unlock) and when reading (achievement check), making the key contract explicit and testable.

findings.description: check_grand_council and check_walking_library call load_unified_save() on every trigger event to count unlocked items, departing from the BattleEndedMessage pattern where all needed data is carried in the message snapshot. Hides an implicit dependency on save-cache consistency.
findings.recommendation: Embed the total unlocked count in WizardTypeUnlockedMessage and SpellResearchedMessage, or maintain a simple counter resource incremented on each unlock, to make the data flow explicit.

findings.description: The near closure (float equality within 0.05 tolerance) is load-bearing logic determining which modifier achievements unlock. It is inlined as a closure with no test coverage. A boundary-case bug would silently prevent achievements from firing.
findings.recommendation: Extract near as a named pub(super) fn approx_eq(a: f32, b: f32) -> bool and add unit tests covering boundary conditions (e.g., 1.0 - 0.049 must pass, 1.0 - 0.051 must fail).

findings.description: detect_out_of_range filters Team::Defenders imperatively inside the loop body rather than using a query filter, so it scans all attacker and undead entities unnecessarily every frame during gameplay until the OutOfRange achievement fires.
findings.recommendation: Use a typed query filter to include only defenders, avoiding iteration over non-defender entities. The achievement_locked gate already stops this system early in most runs.

findings.description: buff_defender_damage and buff_defender_resistance only insert the component when absent (existing.is_none()), never updating it. When multiple Mistletoe/Wormwood brews stack in active_buffs, the summed scalar grows but the already-inserted component retains the first brew's value. The combat system reads the component value directly, so subsequent stacks silently under-buff. Same issue in buff_defender_resistance at line 65.
findings.recommendation: Change the guard from `if existing.is_none()` to `if existing.map(|m| m.0) != Some(bonus)`, matching the already-correct live-update pattern used in apply_cauldron_speed_modifiers (line 139).

findings.description: CAULDRON_COOP_POSITION is byte-for-byte identical to CAULDRON_POSITION (both compute WIZARD_POSITION + CAULDRON_OFFSET). It exists only as a semantic alias. Any future tweak to the co-op position requires remembering to change this constant and not the base one.
findings.recommendation: Delete CAULDRON_COOP_POSITION, replace all call sites with CAULDRON_POSITION, and add a comment at CAULDRON_POSITION noting it is also used as the co-op shared position.

findings.description: CauldronState::Cooldown is suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)] and its tick arm immediately transitions to Idle — the variant is never constructed anywhere in the codebase. The dead arm and the allow attribute signal intentional abandonment while adding ongoing noise.
findings.recommendation: Remove the Cooldown variant and its tick arm. Track any planned brew-cooldown feature in the issue tracker rather than as a dead branch in production code.

findings.description: const MAX_SHIELD: f32 = 20.0 is defined twice as a local constant (also in multiplayer.rs:121) and the shield-keepalive literal 5.0 appears four times across the two files. These shared magic numbers should live in constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Move MAX_SHIELD and the shield-keepalive duration to cauldron/constants.rs as named pub(super) constants and reference them from both shield_defenders and apply_guest_army_buffs.

findings.description: Section divider comment '===== New Ingredient Configs =====' is stale. The ingredients it labels are fully shipped and identical in status to the original set. The label implies they are tentative or recently added, misleading future contributors.
findings.recommendation: Remove or rename the divider to reflect current content (e.g., '===== Extended Ingredients =====').

findings.description: save_unified(&save_file) silently swallows I/O errors. The inner save_unified_save returns ConfigResult<()> but the public wrapper logs and discards failures. The combo-unlock write is fire-and-forget with no call-site acknowledgement.
findings.recommendation: Add a warn! in the storage layer's error path, or at minimum add a comment at this call site acknowledging that the swallowed error is intentional and why.

findings.description: xz_distance is re-defined as a local closure in apply_spell_damage_to_rocks, duplicating the free function of the same name already in scope via crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils (used by terrain/utils.rs). Two implementations of the same function in the same module tree.
findings.recommendation: Remove the local closure and add `use crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils::xz_distance;` at the top of combat.rs.

findings.description: apply_burning_bush_damage and apply_burning_tree_damage (tree/systems.rs:105) are structural clones — identical loop shape, timer tick, heat-radius computation, and apply_heat_zone_fire_dot call. Only component types and three constants differ.
findings.recommendation: Extract an apply_burning_vegetation_damage helper into terrain/utils.rs accepting center, radius, tick_interval, heat_radius_mult, and spell_damage. Both systems become thin wrappers.

findings.description: emit_burning_bush_vfx and emit_burning_tree_vfx (tree/systems.rs:140) are near-identical: same Local timer pattern, same interval logic, same emit_burning_vfx call. Only smoke/spark counts and the height source differ.
findings.recommendation: Extract an emit_burning_vegetation_vfx helper into terrain/utils.rs accepting center, height, radius, smoke_count, spark_count, and interval constants. The two systems reduce to thin wrappers.

findings.description: File names fish.rs and lily.rs in pond/systems/ are misleading. fish.rs contains tick_pond_shocked (electrical arc logic, nothing to do with fish). lily.rs contains apply_pond_wet, tick_wet_timer, apply_frozen_pond_slow (wet/slow logic, nothing to do with lily pads). New readers must open both files to understand pond behavior.
findings.recommendation: Rename fish.rs to shocked.rs and lily.rs to wet_slow.rs. Update pond/systems/mod.rs accordingly.

findings.description: Circle-geometry methods (contains_point_xz, line_segment_intersects, push_out, any_blocks_los) are fully duplicated between Boulder and Tree components. A third copy exists in wizard/spells/wall_of_stone/components.rs — three independent implementations of the same algorithm.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a CircleObstacle { center: Vec3, radius: f32 } newtype in terrain/utils.rs and move the shared methods there. Boulder and Tree can embed or Deref to it. Coordinate with the wall_of_stone scope to eliminate the third copy.

findings.description: Magic number `let start_y = 20.0;` for the vertical boulder launch height has no named constant and no comment explaining its derivation relative to unit sprite heights.
findings.recommendation: Extract `pub(super) const BOULDER_LAUNCH_Y: f32 = 20.0;` into boulder/constants.rs with a comment explaining the intent (e.g. approximate thrower shoulder height in world units).

findings.description: Pond carries ripple_timer: f32, a purely visual emission counter, inside the same component as gameplay-authoritative fields (center, radius). The timer is mutated every ripple-emission interval, marking Pond as Changed and potentially triggering false change-detection in future systems querying Pond.
findings.recommendation: Move ripple_timer to a separate PondRippleTimer component, or store it in a Local<HashMap<Entity, f32>> inside emit_pond_ripples, keeping Pond clean for change-detection purposes.

findings.description: systems.rs is a four-line re-export shim (pub use super::setup::*) whose only purpose is to let external callers spell pathfinding::systems::initialize_pathfinding and pathfinding::systems::suppress_staging_targeting. This is non-idiomatic: mod.rs is the conventional re-export hub, and the indirection obscures where symbols actually live.
findings.recommendation: Remove systems.rs. Move its two re-exports into mod.rs. Update the three external call-sites (plugin.rs line 199, loading/queue.rs line 368, multiplayer/loading.rs line 398).

findings.description: ObstacleChanged.rebuild: bool is marked #[allow(dead_code)] and its own doc comment says it is no longer needed but kept for API compatibility. handle_obstacle_events never reads it. The field is hardcoded to false at 15+ call sites and true at 3 (wall-of-fire) with no observable effect, creating silent contract drift.
findings.recommendation: Remove the rebuild field from ObstacleChanged. Drop rebuild: false from ~15 construction sites. The three rebuild: true sites in wall_of_fire need no replacement since continuous rebuilds already pick up cost changes.

findings.description: PathfindingGrid.world_max: Vec2 carries #[allow(dead_code)]. It is used only during construction to compute grid_width and grid_height, which are stored separately. After construction, world_max is never read.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field. The derived grid dimensions already stored on the struct are what callers need.

findings.description: check_wave_activation allocates a HashMap<u32,(u32,u32)> and a HashSet<u32> on every frame while any staging attackers are alive (potentially hundreds of frames per wave). The early-exit at line 97 covers the post-activation steady state, but during active staging these allocations happen every frame.
findings.recommendation: Declare both collections as Local<HashMap<...>> and Local<HashSet<...>> system parameters and call .clear() at the start of each invocation to reuse the heap allocation across frames.

findings.description: smooth_with_lic performs a full O(N) scan of the costs array on every call (self.costs.iter().any(|&c| c > 1.0 && !c.is_infinite())) to decide whether to skip smoothing. For a field with no elevated terrain this scans every cell to immediately return false, paying full cost to confirm nothing needs doing.
findings.recommendation: Track whether elevated terrain exists as a bool flag on FlowField, set when costs are applied in create_field_with_base_costs. Skip the linear scan by checking the flag instead.

findings.description: WaveStagingPlan::next_staging_point panics via expect() if called before compute_wave_staging. The only caller (tag_new_attackers) lazily initializes the plan first, so the invariant holds in practice, but the method is pub and any future caller that forgets the precondition will get a production panic.
findings.recommendation: Return Option<u8> and let callers handle the missing-plan case, or replace the expect() with a debug_assert! and a safe fallback (e.g. return CENTER_STAGING_INDEX as u8). The project convention forbids production unwrap/expect except for invariants.

findings.description: The doc-comment on generate_initial_fields reads 'Initializes the pathfinding grid resource and registers static terrain obstacles' — which is the description of initialize_pathfinding, not this function. generate_initial_fields only triggers the first attacker field rebuild when the Defender King spawns.
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc-comment to: 'Spawns the initial attacker flow field rebuild task when the Defender King first appears.'

findings.description: compute_wave_staging, WaveStagingPlan::next_staging_point, and check_wave_activation contain core wave distribution and activation logic that directly affects gameplay pacing. flow_field.rs has tests; wave_staging.rs has none.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests covering: correct staging point counts per tunnel, round-robin cycling through chosen points, timeout-based force-activation, and swordcerer avatar aggro activation.

findings.description: plugin.rs defines LensingLabel, HeatDistortionLabel, CrtEffectLabel (three RenderLabel structs), CrtEffectNode struct, and a full ViewNode implementation body — substantial logic beyond registration. Project rule: plugin.rs = registration only.
findings.recommendation: Move CrtEffectLabel, LensingLabel, HeatDistortionLabel, and CrtEffectNode (with ViewNode impl) to pipeline/effect_nodes.rs alongside LensingNode and HeatDistortionNode. plugin.rs imports and registers them.

findings.description: accessibility_nodes.rs hosts five main-world game systems: update_crt_time, sync_colorblind_settings, sync_crt_enabled, sync_high_contrast, sync_flicker_intensity. These are CPU-side config-sync systems, not render node or pipeline code. Makes them hard to find when debugging CRT behavior.
findings.recommendation: Move these five functions to systems.rs or a new sync.rs sibling. accessibility_nodes.rs should contain only ColorblindCorrectionNode, HighContrastNode, and their RenderLabel types.

findings.description: The doc comment on handle_screen_flash_message reads 'Projects active black hole positions to viewport-local UV space for gravitational lensing. The CRT shader operates in viewport-local UV...' — a paste from the lensing function that was never updated. The actual function starts a screen-flash timer.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Reads ScreenFlashMessage and starts (or replaces) the screen-flash animation.'

findings.description: let count = 0u32; in update_lensing_positions is a dead variable. Slots 0-1 were previously used for black-hole lensing and are now permanently zeroed. The variable is only used as a fallback in the max_slot expression where 0u32 literal would suffice. Will generate unused_variable warnings under stricter lints.
findings.recommendation: Remove the variable; inline 0u32 in the max_slot expression. Update the comment at line 98 to note slots 0-1 are permanently disabled.

findings.description: correct_ui_interaction_for_barrel allocates a Vec<(Entity, Vec2)> on the heap every PreUpdate frame it runs (each frame barrel is active). The game has one camera in practice.
findings.recommendation: Replace with camera_query.iter().find_map(...) to avoid heap allocation for the single-camera case. If multiple cameras are a real concern, use SmallVec<[_; 2]>.

findings.description: correct_cursor_for_barrel_distortion runs every PreUpdate with no run_if guard. It short-circuits internally but still pays scheduler and query overhead before the camera is spawned. Every other Update/PreUpdate system in this module has an explicit run_if guard per project convention.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(any_with_component::<CrtEffectSettings>) — the same guard used by update_crt_time.

findings.description: TeleportDistortionPipeline and init_teleport_distortion_pipeline live in accessibility_pipeline.rs alongside colorblind-correction and high-contrast pipelines. Teleport distortion is a gameplay visual effect, not an accessibility feature. The misplacement is also visible in pipeline/mod.rs which re-exports it from accessibility_pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Move TeleportDistortionPipeline and init_teleport_distortion_pipeline to crt_pipeline.rs or a new distortion_pipeline.rs alongside the other effect pipelines (lensing, heat).

findings.description: All four timer types (ChannelChangeTimer, ScreenFlashTimer, VignettePulseTimer, DesaturationTimer) each independently implement an identical sine-bell intensity() + is_finished() pattern (~8 lines each). Any future change to the timing curve requires four parallel edits.
findings.recommendation: Extract struct SineTimer { elapsed: f32, duration: f32 } with tick(), t(), and is_finished() helpers. Each public timer delegates to it, reducing duplication to one location.

findings.description: SpawnTask::Castle is a no-op match arm. The variant is enqueued at init/world_setup.rs:79 but performs zero work because castle geometry is already spawned inside setup_battlefield. Dead variant with empty arm.
findings.recommendation: Remove the Castle variant from SpawnTask, its push_back at world_setup.rs:79, and its empty match arm. Add the ordering comment before the Battlefield arm instead.

findings.description: The wildcard _ arm of match tier % BOSS_CYCLE_LENGTH silently spawns an Ogre but is unreachable. The outer guard !is_lich_level(level) already excludes residue 1, so all five residues (0-4) are covered by named arms or excluded. The wildcard hides future boss-cycle expansion errors.
findings.recommendation: Replace _ => with 1 => unreachable!("lich levels are excluded by the outer guard") to match the canonical boss_name_for_level match and surface bugs if BOSS_CYCLE_LENGTH changes.

findings.description: Each of the six Select*Upgrades match arms (lines 371, 394, 417, 439, 461, 483) re-declares let level = current_level.0; let seed_base = level as u64; identically — 12 duplicate let-bindings inside the while loop on an immutable resource.
findings.recommendation: Hoist both bindings above the while !spawn_queue.is_complete() loop at line 132.

findings.description: apply_commander_upgrade declares _materials: &mut Assets<StandardMaterial> and _meshes: &mut Assets<Mesh> (underscore-prefixed, never read). Callers in queue.rs and wave_systems.rs must pass these assets solely to satisfy the dead parameters.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two unused parameters and update both call sites (queue.rs:558-559 and wave_systems.rs).

findings.description: UpgradeToElite (line 513) and UpgradeToCommander (line 551) arms both manually copy transform and hitbox via sequential ParamSet access with identical boilerplate. The shared helper upgrade_systems::get_transform_and_hitbox exists for this and is already used in wave_systems.rs but not here.
findings.recommendation: Call upgrade_systems::get_transform_and_hitbox in both arms to eliminate the duplicated copy pattern.

findings.description: Step-numbering comments are inconsistent: '// 8. Defender Archers' appears at line 343 after step 8 was already used at line 263 for attacker archers; both cauldron steps are labelled '// 13.'; steps 7, 9, 10 are skipped.
findings.recommendation: Renumber step comments to match actual queue order, or drop numbering in favor of descriptive inline comments.

findings.description: systems.rs is a single-line stale comment referencing an internal refactor phase ('Phase 18') with no exported symbols. The module is declared in mod.rs but is entirely dead.
findings.recommendation: Delete systems.rs and remove its mod systems; declaration from mod.rs.

findings.description: The doc-comment on process_spawn_queue reads 'Initializes the loading progress tracker and spawn queue' — copied from the old monolith before init.rs was split out. It describes init_loading_progress, not this function.
findings.recommendation: Update the doc-comment to describe per-frame spawn queue draining.

findings.description: Lines 198-199 contain inner use crate::game::constants::{BOSS_CYCLE_LENGTH, get_tier} and use crate::game::constants::{is_boss_level, is_lich_level} inside the function body. These symbols are already in scope from the module-level glob use crate::game::constants::* at line 7. The re-imports are redundant noise.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two inner use statements.

findings.description: cursor_position: Option<Vec2> is present on MouseLeftPressed, MouseLeftHeld, MouseRightPressed, and MouseRightHeld (lines 13, 21, 33, 41), all suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)]. A codebase-wide search confirms the field is never read by any consumer — all downstream spell systems read CorrectedCursorPosition directly. The field is populated at write sites but silently discarded, creating a misleading contract.
findings.recommendation: Remove the cursor_position field from all four message structs and all write sites in systems.rs (lines 80, 84, 99, 103) and gamepad/systems/navigation.rs (lines 58, 66–67, 72, 87–88, 91).

findings.description: detect_rune_input uses fully qualified 5-segment paths (crate::game::units::wizard::archetypes::runes::messages::RunePressed repeated 3x, crate::game::units::wizard::archetypes::runes::resources::Rune 4x) while detect_roulette_input repeats the full RouletteSpinMessage path twice. The existing use imports at the top of the file are not used for these types, cluttering the function bodies.
findings.recommendation: Add use imports for RunePressed, ActivateRuneSequence, Rune, and RouletteSpinMessage at the top of systems.rs, matching the clean import style already established in gamepad/action_translation.rs.

findings.description: ActionBarKeyPressed.slot documentation says '0-9, where 0 represents the 10th slot' but the implementation in detect_keyboard_input only binds 5 slots (indices 0–4) and RADIAL_SLOT_COUNT is 5. The doc is aspirational/stale relative to the current code.
findings.recommendation: Update the field doc to '0–4, mapping to the five action bar slots' or, if 10-slot expansion is planned, add an explicit note marking it as a reserved future range.

findings.description: The comment on translate_runes states the activate action is 'handled by the keyboard-side detect_rune_input which consumes SpacebarPressed.' This is factually wrong: detect_rune_input reads ButtonInput<KeyCode> directly and never reads the SpacebarPressed message. The comment misleads anyone tracing the gamepad rune-activation code path.
findings.recommendation: Correct the comment: detect_rune_input polls the keyboard binding directly and emits ActivateRuneSequence; translate_activate_button independently emits SpacebarPressed from the South button.

findings.description: detect_active_input_device computes mag_sq.sqrt() to compare against DEVICE_SWITCH_STICK_MAGNITUDE (0.25). The sqrt is unnecessary — comparing mag_sq > threshold * threshold is mathematically identical and avoids the float sqrt on every PreUpdate frame.
findings.recommendation: Replace mag_sq.sqrt() > DEVICE_SWITCH_STICK_MAGNITUDE with mag_sq > DEVICE_SWITCH_STICK_MAGNITUDE * DEVICE_SWITCH_STICK_MAGNITUDE.

findings.description: tick_wizard_cycle handles per-archetype UI spawning but is missing Meteorologist. The meteorologist plugin spawns weather overlays and a ground overlay on OnEnter(InGameState::Running); those systems don't re-fire when config.wizard_type changes mid-game. Cycling TO Meteorologist leaves weather visuals absent; cycling AWAY leaves overlays orphaned.
findings.recommendation: Add a WizardType::Meteorologist arm to call spawn_weather_overlays and spawn_ground_overlay, and add cleanup of weather overlay entities when departing from Meteorologist. Consider extracting per-archetype setup/teardown into a wizard_cycle_ui.rs sibling file.

findings.description: tick_wizard_cycle is 106 lines and encodes archetype-specific UI spawning inline. As archetypes are added, every author must remember to add a branch here AND keep it in sync with each archetype's own plugin. The catch-all comment is the only guard against omissions.
findings.recommendation: Extract wizard-cycle UI management into a wizard_cycle_ui.rs sibling file. Keep tick_wizard_cycle focused on the timer logic; the per-archetype dispatch table becomes easy to audit in isolation.

findings.description: animate_fortified_horde_glow calls shielded.is_empty() and returns early, but the system is already gated with .run_if(any_exist::<FortifiedHordeShield>()) in the plugin. The guard can never be true when the system fires — it is dead code.
findings.recommendation: Remove the if shielded.is_empty() { return; } guard at line 221.

findings.description: Unlocked wizard types are compared using format!("{:?}", wt), coupling the on-disk save format to Rust's Debug output. A rename of any WizardType variant silently breaks unlock detection with no compiler warning.
findings.recommendation: Add an fn id(&self) -> &'static str method on WizardType (mirroring ToggleModifier::id()) and use it in wizard_crud.rs, save_structs.rs, and systems.rs:60 for all wizard-type string keys.

findings.description: When load_unified_save() fails in init_toggle_resources, WizardCycle silently treats all wizard types as locked (empty unlocked_types), causing the toggle to appear non-functional with no diagnostic output.
findings.recommendation: Add warn!("WizardCycle: failed to load save data; treating all wizard types as locked") on the failure path before unwrap_or_default().

findings.description: Approximately 30 types that should be top-level use imports are embedded as bare super::super::super::... paths directly inside the Query<(...)> parameter type (lines 34-108). The function signature spans ~95 lines and is nearly unreadable because none of the spell-modifier component types have named imports.
findings.recommendation: Convert all inline super::super::super::... paths inside the query/system parameters to top-level 'use crate::game::...' import statements. This is a purely mechanical rename with no behaviour change.

findings.description: ~40 inline super::super::super::... paths are scattered through the function signature, body, and .remove::<...>() chain (lines 26-305). Mixed with 8 top-level 'use crate::game::...' imports, there is no consistent rule distinguishing which types get named imports.
findings.recommendation: Replace every inline super-chain with named 'use crate::game::...' imports at the top of the file, matching the style already used for the achievement message imports.

findings.description: combat() is a 500-line god function handling: snapshot collection, attack-timer evaluation, fog-redirect logic, per-target health query with 14-field tuple, 11 separate damage-modifier chains, animation triggering, bloodlust accumulation, contagious-rage kill tracking, and deferred action flushing. Convention requires files >300 LOC to be split unless cohesive.
findings.recommendation: Extract at minimum: resolve_damage_modifiers() for the ~100-line modifier chain, redirect_for_disorienting_vapors() for the fog-zone redirect, and flush_post_combat_actions() for the deferred action loop. These can remain in the same file as free functions called from the main system.

findings.description: The corpse conversion system manually removes ~40 components via a hand-maintained .remove::<T>() chain (lines 246-305). When a new status-effect component is added to the game it is easy to omit from this list, leaving dead units with stale components that could affect subsequent frames.
findings.recommendation: Extract a helper function remove_all_status_effects(entity_cmds: &mut EntityCommands) in units/status_effects.rs or units/components.rs so every death-cleanup path is co-located. The system calls the helper once instead of maintaining its own list.

findings.description: The module doc says 'Post-combat reactions: invulnerability and corpse conversion' but the file names are swapped relative to what they contain: cleanup.rs holds the corpse conversion logic and death_conversion.rs holds the invulnerability enforcement — the opposite of what their names imply.
findings.recommendation: Rename cleanup.rs to corpse_conversion.rs and death_conversion.rs to invulnerability.rs, then update the mod doc. Purely cosmetic but prevents future contributors from opening the wrong file.

findings.description: flying_set is allocated as a HashSet<Entity> every frame even when no flying units are present in the current wave. The allocation is unnecessary when the set would be empty.
findings.recommendation: Guard with flying_units.is_empty() before collecting; skip the HashSet allocation when no flying units exist.

findings.description: The disorienting-vapors redirect iterates units_snapshot twice per affected attacker: once to .count() and once to .nth(idx). This is O(2n) per attacker in a fog zone.
findings.recommendation: Collect the filtered same-team subslice into a local Vec once, then index by random position directly. Allocation is bounded by unit count and only happens when the fog spell is active.

findings.description: DISORIENTING_VAPORS_CHANCE is referenced via a 9-segment inline path (super::super::super::units::wizard::spells::fog_cloud::constants::DISORIENTING_VAPORS_CHANCE) without a use import, while all other fog_cloud types in the same file do have use imports at the top.
findings.recommendation: Add 'use crate::game::units::wizard::spells::fog_cloud::constants::DISORIENTING_VAPORS_CHANCE;' at the top of the file.

findings.description: CLOSE_CALL_DISTANCE is imported from swordcerer::constants inside a use statement within the function body. This constant controls proximity-to-wizard kill tracking, which is a generic achievement trigger not specific to the swordcerer archetype, creating misleading module ownership.
findings.recommendation: Move CLOSE_CALL_DISTANCE to an achievements constants module or inline the value with a comment. This removes a dependency on a wizard-archetype module from the post-combat cleanup path.

findings.description: systems.rs (640 LOC) mixes three unrelated concerns: spawn/setup helpers (lines 1–396), environmental VFX emitters (lines 398–640), and terrain hazard gameplay systems. The project convention requires splitting any file >300 LOC that contains multiple concerns.
findings.recommendation: Split into spawn.rs (setup_battlefield, spawn helpers, ground tiles), vfx.rs (lava smoke/sparks, water ripples, ambient motes), and hazards.rs (apply_lava_damage, apply_water_slow). Update mod.rs and plugin.rs imports accordingly.

findings.description: emit_water_ripples allocates a brand-new StandardMaterial asset on every ripple spawn (every WATER_RIPPLE_INTERVAL = 1.2 s). Because Bevy's asset store is reference-counted and despawning the ripple entity drops the handle, the material is eventually freed—but this causes repeated GPU-side material registration/deallocation cycles.
findings.recommendation: Pre-allocate a small Vec<Handle<StandardMaterial>> of blank ripple materials in WaterRippleAssets at startup; recycle them by updating alpha via materials.get_mut instead of creating new assets per ripple.

findings.description: sync_trampling_texture allocates a fresh Vec<u8> (up to ~256 KB for a 256x256 grid) every sync interval (~0.25 s) even when only a few cells changed. The vec is discarded after one use.
findings.recommendation: Pre-allocate the pixel buffer once as a Local<Vec<u8>> in the system and reuse it each sync.

findings.description: let assets = ripple_assets; inside emit_water_ripples is a stale no-op alias that adds nothing. Appears to be a leftover rename artefact.
findings.recommendation: Remove the alias; replace the downstream use (assets.mesh.clone()) with ripple_assets.mesh.clone().

findings.description: Three magic-number offsets (+100.0, -100.0, -1500.0) are used inline in setup_battlefield when positioning the sand and stone noise underlay meshes. They relate to visual alignment but are completely undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Extract named constants (e.g. SAND_UNDERLAY_OFFSET_X, SAND_UNDERLAY_OFFSET_Z, STONE_UNDERLAY_Z) to constants.rs with short comments explaining what they align to.

findings.description: TramplingGrid::world_to_index is non-trivial coordinate math (boundary clamping, row-major index calculation) with no unit tests. The analogous pathfinding grid coordinate math has historically been a source of off-by-one bugs.
findings.recommendation: Add an inline #[cfg(test)] module testing boundary cases: coords at -half, +half, 0, and outside-bounds inputs.

findings.description: The 120-frame entity-cleanup path in track_unit_trampling allocates a fresh HashSet<Entity> every 120 frames unconditionally, even in stable battles where no entity has recently despawned.
findings.recommendation: Guard the HashSet allocation behind a cheap check (e.g. compare last_cells.len() against units.iter().count()) or use a despawn-event driven path.

findings.description: Plugin doc comment says 'the F3 toggle' but systems.rs:14 binds KeyCode::F4. Wrong key in docs misleads anyone using benchmarking builds.
findings.recommendation: Change the doc comment on BenchmarkingPlugin::build to say 'F4 toggle'.

findings.description: IngredientDrop::time_alive is documented as 'for despawn and fade' but no fade or timeout-despawn logic exists anywhere; time_alive is used only for bobbing/pulse animation math.
findings.recommendation: Update the field doc to 'for bobbing and pulse animation'. If a timeout-despawn is desired, add a DROP_MAX_LIFETIME constant and a despawn branch to tick_drop_lifetimes.

findings.description: toggle_diagnostics registers unconditionally in Update with no run_if guard. Per project conventions every Update system needs a run_if. Only relevant in benchmarking feature builds so shipping impact is zero, but it breaks the convention.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(not(diagnostics_enabled)) or a state-based guard so the convention is maintained even in the special benchmark build.

findings.description: init_game_seed is declared pub but is only called from the sibling plugin.rs. pub(super) is the correct visibility per project conventions.
findings.recommendation: Change `pub fn init_game_seed` to `pub(super) fn init_game_seed`.

findings.description: derive_seed multiplies by purpose as its final step, so purpose = 0 collapses the entire output to 0 regardless of master seed or level. All three current SEED_PURPOSE_* constants are prime and non-zero, but there is no guard preventing a future zero constant from silently producing a degenerate seed.
findings.recommendation: Add debug_assert_ne!(purpose, 0, "derive_seed: purpose constant must be non-zero") or reorder the arithmetic so purpose is not the sole final multiplier.

findings.description: sync_achievements_to_steam is registered to Update with no run_if guard, violating project convention. It calls client.user_stats() — a non-trivial FFI call — every frame even when no AchievementUnlockedMessage is pending.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(on_event::<AchievementUnlockedMessage>()) or an equivalent message-based condition to avoid the per-frame FFI call when idle.

findings.description: Eight Update systems (process_create_lobby_result, process_join_lobby_result, process_lobby_chat_updates, process_game_lobby_join_requested, process_game_rich_presence_join_requested, consume_pending_join_in_main_menu, drive_steam_listen_socket, poll_steam_guest_connection_state) run every frame with no run_if guard, violating project convention. Each has an inline early-return so they are cheap-when-idle, but the overhead accumulates.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the entire block with .run_if(resource_exists::<SteamLobbyBridge>) as a proxy for Steam MP initialized. steam_transport_bridge_system self-gates on ConnectionMode::Steam but still needs an outer run_if.

findings.description: sync_save_to_steam_cloud silently discards std::fs::read failure with bare Err(_) => return. When no local save exists this is correct, but any other error (permissions, path issue) is swallowed with no log line.
findings.recommendation: Use Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return for the expected case, and add a warn! for all other errors before returning.

findings.description: join_lobby_rx: Receiver<Result<LobbyId, ()>> uses unit error because upstream bevy_steamworks join_lobby returns Result<LobbyId, ()>. The loss of the concrete error means process_join_lobby_result can only log a generic failure message.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment explaining that () mirrors the upstream API shape so future readers don't try to enrich the type and discover the constraint. Update if bevy_steamworks exposes an error type in a future version.

findings.description: Two Startup-phase system bodies (init_steam_lobby_bridge, init_relay_network_access) live in a file named lobby_systems.rs, which readers expect to contain Update-phase systems. Breaks the implicit naming contract.
findings.recommendation: Move the two Startup system bodies to a new startup.rs sibling file, consistent with the project's feature-sliced convention.

findings.description: Module-level doc says 'P2P WebRTC communication' and 'WebRTC with copy-paste SDP signaling'. The transport was replaced with iroh/QUIC; no WebRTC or SDP exists in the current code.
findings.recommendation: Replace with 'P2P QUIC communication using iroh' and remove the SDP sentence.

findings.description: ConnectionState::WaitingForSignaling doc says 'SDP exchange complete'; local_code field doc (line 61) says 'Base64-encoded SDP+ICE code'. Both reference the old WebRTC signaling model. iroh uses a direct endpoint-address ticket, not SDP/ICE.
findings.recommendation: Update ConnectionState::WaitingForSignaling doc to 'Waiting for the user to exchange connection codes' and local_code doc to 'Base64-encoded iroh endpoint address'.

findings.description: File doc header (line 3) and NetworkMessage doc comment (line 70) both say 'WebRTC data channels'.
findings.recommendation: Update to 'QUIC streams'.

findings.description: Three stale doc items: (1) file header says 'unreliable WebRTC data channel'; (2) UnitSnapshot has an orphan leading doc line '/// Per-unit state with CRDT health data (~37 bytes).' on line 33 immediately before the real doc paragraph on line 34 — a leftover from a prior edit; (3) SpellArcSnapshot::kind doc (line 481) lists '6=Disintegrate' which the collector comment confirms is no longer emitted (Disintegrate now ships via BeamSnapshot).
findings.recommendation: Fix file header; remove orphan line 33; drop '6=Disintegrate' from arc kind doc or annotate as legacy-receive-only.

findings.description: fragment_datagram caps fragment_count at 255 via .min(255) as u8, but then iterates ALL chunks. If the payload ever requires more than 255 fragments (~305 KB at 1200-byte datagrams), fragments at index >=255 have i as u8 == 255, which is out-of-bounds in the 255-slot fragments array — the receiver's bounds check silently drops them, truncating the payload with no error. Current snapshot sizes (~24 KB max, 21 fragments) never trigger this, but it is a latent silent-truncation trap.
findings.recommendation: Truncate the iterator to fragment_count items (.take(fragment_count as usize)) and add a warn! if chunks.len() > 255 so the limit surfaces clearly if payloads grow.

findings.description: build_unit_snapshot takes 21 parameters, 14 of which are plain bool. A caller swap (e.g. has_fire and has_frost) is invisible to the compiler.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a UnitFlagSources { is_corpse: bool, is_king: bool, ... } struct so the call site is self-documenting and positional swaps become compile errors.

findings.description: connection.rs imports tracing::warn directly; all other networking files and the entire game codebase use bevy::log macros from bevy::prelude::*. bevy::log macros are thin wrappers over tracing and work fine in the tokio background thread.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'use tracing::warn;' with 'use bevy::prelude::*;' to unify the logging API surface.

findings.description: SpellArcSnapshot::kind doc lists kinds 0,1,4,5,6. Kinds 2 (crystal_beam) and 3 (crystal_arc) are handled by the receiver in ghost_spawn.rs but are never emitted by the current sender — projectile_collect.rs migrated them to other paths. The receiver arms are dead code and the doc is inconsistent with both sender and receiver.
findings.recommendation: Update the kind doc to enumerate all 6 variants (0-5, drop 6) and annotate 2 and 3 as 'receiver-only legacy arms, not currently emitted'.

findings.description: transport_bridge_system runs in PreUpdate every frame with no run_if guard. The system has an internal early-out but is still scheduled unconditionally including in menus and single-player. Project convention requires all Update-schedule systems to carry run_if.
findings.recommendation: Add run_if(resource_exists::<TransportHandle>) or a connection-active condition.

findings.description: UnitSnapshot.max_hp ships on every frame for every unit. The comment on line 69 acknowledges this ('could be thinned later via a separate one-shot spawn message'). At 200 units this is ~800 extra bytes/frame on the unreliable channel.
findings.recommendation: Deferred optimization: when snapshot size becomes a bottleneck, introduce a reliable spawn message carrying max_hp once and remove it from UnitSnapshot.

findings.description: Seven debug-logging systems are registered unconditionally in Update with no run_if guard. Each runs every frame and checks Res::is_changed() internally. Project convention requires every Update system to carry a run_if guard. Bevy 0.18 ships state_changed::<S>() in bevy_state::condition for exactly this pattern.
findings.recommendation: Replace each registration with .run_if(state_changed::<S>()), e.g. log_app_state_transitions.run_if(state_changed::<AppState>()). This eliminates seven per-frame resource fetches and aligns with the project run_if policy.

findings.description: log_app_state_transitions takes Res<State<AppState>> (non-Optional), while all six other logging systems take Option<Res<State<...>>>. The asymmetry is correct but unexplained — a reader trap implying the other states might not exist for an undocumented reason.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief comment on line 12 explaining that AppState is always registered (init_state) so Option<> is unnecessary, or make all seven Option<Res<...>> for visual uniformity.

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] on AppState (line 19) and MenuState (line 56) with comment 'Variants will be used as game features are implemented.' All 7 AppState variants and all 4 MenuState variants are actively referenced in the codebase. The suppressors are stale and could mask genuinely dead variants in future.
findings.recommendation: Remove both #[allow(dead_code)] attributes.

findings.description: Three doc examples (lines 25, 42, 58) use 'use court_wizard::state::AppState' — a public crate path that does not exist. The crate is a binary (src/main.rs; no src/lib.rs), so the court_wizard:: namespace is inaccessible. cargo test --doc would fail on these examples.
findings.recommendation: Change use paths in doc examples to 'use crate::state::AppState' or add a '# fn main() {}' wrapper noting these are illustrative only.

findings.description: MetaGameState has exactly one variant (WizardTower). A single-variant sub-state provides no discriminated behavior — all code conditioning on in_state(MetaGameState::WizardTower) is equivalent to in_state(AppState::MetaGame). The sub-state incurs registration cost and a pointless import in every consuming file.
findings.recommendation: Either add the anticipated additional variants now (e.g. StudyDesk, Talents) or collapse this sub-state and use AppState::MetaGame directly until a second variant is genuinely needed.

findings.description: process_music_fade queries &mut AudioSink directly, but Bevy adds AudioSink to an AudioPlayer entity one frame after spawn (audio backend processes asynchronously). Entities spawned in the same frame are silently skipped by the query, losing the first timer tick with no volume set. Implicit timing assumption with no documentation.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment documenting the one-frame delay. Optionally use Option<&mut AudioSink> and continue explicitly so the skip is visible in code.

findings.description: process_music_fade re-reads game_config.effective_music_volume() every tick per fading entity. If the user scrubs the volume slider during a 1.5 s crossfade, the fade target silently shifts mid-interpolation. A fade-out could become louder before quieter if volume is raised during the transition.
findings.recommendation: Add a target_volume: f32 field to MusicFade, snapshot it at spawn time in check_music_transition, and use that snapshotted value in process_music_fade so the fade arc is stable regardless of concurrent config changes.

findings.description: track_for_state has no explicit visibility modifier (defaults to pub(self)). The rest of the module's internal helpers are explicitly marked pub(super) per project convention.
findings.recommendation: Change to pub(super) fn track_for_state to match the module's explicit-visibility convention.

findings.description: When GameConfig is None inside check_music_transition, the function silently returns with no log output. This can cause music to silently fail to start if the resource-added trigger fires before config is loaded.
findings.recommendation: Add warn!("check_music_transition: GameConfig not yet available, skipping") before the early return so the silent skip is observable in logs.

oversized.reason: Mixed concern groups — five distinct categories of status effect components. Not a single registry or match-on-enum monolith.

Two separable concerns: facing direction state (FacingDirection, FacingDwell, FacingHysteresisBoost, SmoothedFacingVelocity) and sprite-sheet animation data (WalkingAnimation, CombatAnimation, DyingAnimation, RisingAnimation, PulsingAnimation).
Purely Bevy registration (add_systems, configure_sets, add_plugins). No logic bodies. The large size reflects extensive inline comments explaining non-obvious MP ordering constraints.
Single large match-on-enum monolith — display names, descriptions, flavour text, compendium sprite specs. Every function is an exhaustive match arm per variant.
Mixed concerns: lifecycle cleanup, gameplay ticks, battle ambience audio, shadow rendering pipeline, achievement tracking
Two functions (tick_wave_timer + apply_wave_upgrades) are tightly coupled by the PendingWaveUpgrades data flow; both operate on the same unit-spawn helpers. No unrelated logic is present.

Single enum with all 31 spells; every public function is a match self { ... } covering all variants. Splitting by concern would scatter a single enum's arms across files with no benefit. Canonical registry monolith.

All content is the CastingState state-machine enum plus directly associated types (PrimedSpell, GlobalCastCooldown, SpellCaster). Every method is a small accessor on the same state machine. Genuinely cohesive.
Borderline at 292 lines but every function is a distinct Bevy system; no single function exceeds ~50 lines. Consistent system-per-function structure; acceptable without a split.
Mixed concerns: avatar spawn receipt, guest input streaming (send + apply), and avatar death lifecycle — 4 distinct networking concerns in one file.
